These studies are designed to create a new way of learning, and to facilitate this learning by using architecture to create environments that support spontaneous and planned collaboration into the architecture of their new and existing buildings.

His other projects include developing virtual architecture for display of large sculptures and extending exhibitions. Some of these designs have been utilized and exhibited in Europe. He is also involved in developing new methods of constructing with recycled material and innovative concrete form work techniques using 3-D computer modeling.

Prior to his architectural work with Maadluxe Design, he worked at Rockwell Group, Arquitectonica and KPF (Kohn Pedersen Fox Associates). His project experience included Research Laboratories, Schools, Master Planning, Town House Design and Development, Multistory Apartment Complexes and Luxury Dwellings.

In his free time Alexander enjoys sketching, hiking, travel and exploring urban environments

title: Professor
bio:
Illya Azaroff, FAIA, is an Architect, Geographer and internationally recognized leader in disaster mitigation, adaptation, regenerative design and resilient planning strategies with over 30 years experience. He is a full tenured professor at New York City College of Technology (CUNY) leading sustainability courses. His research and professional work serve a mission to build resilient capacity and advance goals for a sustainable, regenerative future while giving underserved communities greater voice and visibility. He often works with cities, governing bodies and design teams around the world to build resilient capacity. He serves as a technical expert on the New York Climate Impact Assessment appointed by the governor Hochul, has advised the New York City Mayor Adams transition team and founded the AIA New York Unified Crisis Task Force City & State on issues surrounding COVID19 Pandemic; receiving the 2022 Collaborative Achievement Award from AIA National as well as the Power of A Gold award from ASAE. With the ANCR/ICC – International Code Council he helped develop community resilience benchmarks system. Prior he served as subject mater expert with the Rockefeller Foundation 100RC as well as a Technical Advisor to HHS-ASPR-Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response informing the NDFR-National Disaster Recovery Framework. Given his expertise U.S. State Department has Illya Receive foreign delegations to exchange sustainable and resilient strategies.

He is a founding partner at +LAB Architect PLLC. His work with communities range from New York City housing authority, Houston Texas, Puerto Rico, Bahamas, USVI and the City of Oakland Park Florida. On the island of Dominica he is a founding director of KIGRR the Kalinago Institute of Global Regeneration and Resilience working with the first people of the Island aimed at creating a sustainable, resilient future through a series of cross sector projects including culturally significant resilience hubs, while in Hawai’i creating a resilience hub for the Ko`olauloa community by regenerating a traditional Ahupuaʻa socioeconomic, geologic, and climatic subdivision of land. His studio designed an All-hazard home in Breezy Point New York Hurricane stong home, noted as the “next generation of housing” by the City of New York’s Mayors office of Resilience. He is an instructor with NDTPC-National Disaster Training Preparedness Center out of Hawaii and is certified trainer for post disaster Safety Assessment Program (SAP) through CalEMA (California Emergency Management). Illya is a Fellow of the American Institute of Architects (2021) and a Louise Bethune Fellow (2018), and has served as AIA New York State President 2021 and is thrilled to be elected to the AIA National Board 2023-25. In 2022 Professor Azaroff will be representing the Architects of the United States at Conference of Parties COP 27, in Egypt discussing global commitments to carbon reduction and the impact architects can have on disaster risk reduction across the world.

His work has been published in various magazines and books, including Climate Adaptation and Resilience Across Scales by Routledge, The New York Times, Forbes, Washington Post, Journal of Extreme events and Architect Magazine to name a few. His films and TED talk are widely viewed highlighting his commitment to social impact design. Especially in the wake of Superstorm Sandy, Azaroff was a frequent consultant to New York City and other public entities on issues of resilience, equity and sustainability contributing to NYC The Department of City Planning - Housing Retrofit Guidelines, FLASH - Federal Alliance for Safe Homes, Resilient Housing Guidelines and Enterprise Community Partners Multi-Family Resilient Strategies and Keep Safe: A Guide to Resilient Housing for Island Communities and NYC Resilient Design Guidelines. Prior to New York City he worked in Germany, Italy and Holland. Illya has a Masters in Architecture as well as a Bachelors of Architecture from Pratt Institute and Bachelor of Arts in Geography and Bachelor of Science of Architecture from University of Nebraska at Lincoln.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Bachelor of Architecture - New York Institute of Technology
Bachelor of Architecture - University of Costa Rica
Master of Architecture - University of Tokyo
Doctorate of Architecture - University of Tokyo
Licensed Architect: Federal College of Engineers and Architects of Costa Rica

Dr. Beita is the founder of Wabi Design, a firm specializing in the implementation of traditional Japanese design principles in contemporary architecture. The firm takes its inspiration from Japanese architecture to create architecture that constantly interacts with its environment. His specialties are in design, 3d modeling and Japanese architecture and his professional experience includes high-end residential, commercial, hotel and resorts. His research focuses on the improvement of urban spaces through the use of Japanese traditional design principles.

Dr. Beita is also the recipient of the Monbukagakusho scholarship, a prestigious scholarship offered by the Japanese government. While in Japan, he performed research in the creation of photorealistic 3d models for analyzing the movement of light. He then implemented this research in modeling one of Japans most famous tea rooms, the Bosen Tea Room, to analyzed how traditional design principles function and can be used in western architecture. In a period of six years, Dr. Beita documented over 120 different building types, including: Temples, Tea rooms, Tea houses, Tea schools, Pavilions, Dwellings and Shrines.

Throughout his education, his had the opportunity to study, lecture and work in different parts of the world, ranging from New York, Costa Rica, Russia, Spain and Japan. This has given him a variety of skills in design, sustainable architecture, 3d modeling, photography, architecture visualization, and Japanese design. In Tokyo, Dr. Beita worked and interned for Toyo Ito and Kengo Kuma, while at the same time conducting an extensive research on traditional and contemporary Japanese architecture.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Architectural Technology BA Architecture
Unversity of Washington; BArch and MArch
Pratt Institute NY

Professor Bouratoglou is a licensed Architect and Principal of Bouratoglou Architect, PC. Her practice includes a variety of projects in the New York; including residential and commercial; both new construction and renovations. The practice focuses on simple, clear design.

Professor Bouratoglou won a Society of American Registered Architects Award of Merit in 2005. Her project and article was featured in Fine Homebuilding Houses 2006. A project will also be included in the book "The Simple Home".

title: Chair
bio:
Professor Chin is an Associate Professor and a founding principal of Linearscape, an award-winning interdisciplinary design studio. Linearscape has received prestigious awards, including the AIA Emerging New York Architects Award, an AIA Citation, and a SARA Design Excellence Award. Her teaching, research, and practice engage in exploration and multidisciplinary collaboration to arrive at design solutions inspired by the fluidity of movement and the integration of landscape and context with building form, materials, and systems.

Prior to entering academia and co-founding Linearscape, Professor Chin worked in renowned architectural and landscape design offices, focusing on cultural and educational facilities, as well as public urban spaces. More recently, she has been actively involved in presenting, researching, and writing about interdisciplinary approaches to designing sustainable and symbiotic urban environments, while also investigating pedagogical approaches to design. She earned her Master of Architecture degree from the Graduate School of Design at Harvard University.

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
BArch, New Jersey Institute of Technology
AAGradDipl (MArch), History/Theory Program, The Architectural Association, London, England
SARA/NY, Director
Registered Architect in the State of New York

Ken Conzelmann began teaching at City Tech in 1990 as an adjunct instructor. He discovered that education and practice were distinct, yet interdependent realms, which together offered a potent synergy.

Ken's work explores many fronts with particular interest in cultural context, textural conditions and the physical/psychological dimensions of the architectural experience. He has had the opportunity to participate in a full spectrum of work settings and genres: sole practice and partnership; collaborations with architects, artists and engineers; consultation with small and mid-sized design firms; and employment with large government agency and high profile corporate enterprises. This broad exposure allowed for engagement on a wide range of projects: rural and urban homes, historic row house and apartment renovations; a new bank tower; a 16th century guest house/hotel conversion in Meissen (East) Germany; a short list proposal for a Buddhist temple; a LEED-certified, fully progressive early childhood center, including geothermal heating/cooling mechanics and a garden roof; and an award winning entry for The High Line Design Ideas Competition. This varied and expansive portfolio provides a healthy mix for him to share with students and colleagues.

Professor Conzelmann is director of the Architectural Internship program, teaches 3D Design as an interdisciplinary liaison with ADGA, and continues as a regular guest critic and speaker beyond City Tech. He has studied and worked in England, Germany and Austria and today continues in private practice in downtown Manhattan.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
B.Arch, University of Minnesota
MS in Architecture and Building Design, Columbia University
Certified by the National Council of Architects Registration Board
Registered Architect in the State of New York
Registered Architect in Cyprus

Professor Dikigoropoulou holds a Bachelor of Architecture from the University of Minnesota and a Master of Science in Architecture in Building Design from Columbia University. She has studied traditional Chinese architecture in China and was the team leader for a National Park Service project to document the Blue Ridge Parkway in North Carolina. She is a Registered Architect in both the US and Cyprus and maintains NCARB certification as well. She has experience with a wide range of residential and commercial projects, from brownstone renovations to health clubs and airport terminals, and, in the process, has interacted extensively with the New York City Buildings and Landmarks Preservation Departments.

As a native of Cyprus and a frequent world traveler, she draws from a diverse palette of experiences when devising her solutions to particular architectural challenges. She is the international education liaison for the Department.

Professor Dikigoropoulou is also an accomplished potter.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
M.Arch.: Yale University School of Architecture
B.A.: New York University
Registered Architect: State of New York

Professor Duddy is the Senior Design Principal of DCI Designgroup International, an international architectural practice headquartered in New Yorkwith offices in Shanghai and Beijing. As the managing principal of the New York office, he concentrates on mixed-use commercial developments in Eastern Asia, working closely with Asian clients and directing the DCI design staff in New York and Shanghai.

Professor Duddy has more than thirty years of experience in the planning and design of mixed-use projects worldwide. After completing his studies at the Yale School of Architecture, he joined the firm of Cesar Pelli and Associates in New Haven as an architectural designer, working on large-scale commercial projects that include the World Financial Center in New York, and the award-winning Wells Fargo Center in Minneapolis.

After relocating to New York, he spent eight years at Hellmuth, Obata, and Kassabaum as the Senior Design Associate. Notable among his assignments during his tenure there was his role as senior designer of the Ted Weiss Federal Building in Lower Manhattan, and as a leader of the design team that originated the concept to transform the James Farley Post Office in New York into the new Moynihan Station.

Along with teaching, Professor Duddy continues to pursue research in the areas of architectonic reasoning and visual logic. He is currently doing research on the epistemological foundations of perspective.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
BArch, Pratt Institute
MS Architecture and Urban Design, Columbia University
PhD Esoteric Studies, Albert University
Registered Architect in the State of New York

Professor Edwards has specialized in the design of Television broadcast facilities for the major part of his career. His work involves site selection and analysis, costing, program development, design, detailing, construction documents, and construction administration as senior architect and architect of record for a host of projects. These include NBC's New York Rockefeller Center Hub for the international broadcast of the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, New York News 1, Madison Square Garden Broadcast Center, CW 11 (formerly WPIX, Channel 11), Nickelodeon Studios, CNBC America is Talking, Manhattan Neighborhood Network, USA Networks, PBS (Channel 13), Major League Baseball and National Basketball Association. This work involved extreme attention to detail, product specification, lighting, acoustics, building systems, the integration of television systems, equipment, consoles, sight lines and ergonomics. He developed his own set of construction specifications for this specialized work.

Professor Edwards has been responsible for the gut renovation and design of over 40 multi-family residential, multi-story buildings in Manhattan, Brooklyn and the Bronx. His work included the development of construction documents including architectural structural, plumbing, electrical and sprinkler drawings. He is currently a partner in the firm Breger Bermel Associates, an architectural firm specializing in the design and construction of Health Care Facilities.

Professor Edwards is a national lecturer for various AIA Chapters, where he specializes in the seminar training of architectural interns for the building systems architectural license exam. He was a featured speaker at the 2007 AIA National Convention in San Antonio, Texas, where he lectured on the topic. He has also reviewed architectural training materials for architectural interns developed by Kaplan Architectural Education. Professor Edwards graduated at the very top of his class at both the undergraduate and graduate levels.

title: Associate Professor/B.Arch Co-director
bio:
Claudia currently teaches both at the Department of Architectural Technology at NYCCT and in the Department of Interior Design at Pratt Institute. She holds a Master of Science degree in Advanced Architectural Design from Columbia University and a Bachelor of Architecture from California Polytechnic State University in San Luis Obispo.

For the past ten years she has worked in several design-oriented architecture firms both San Francisco and New York. Her work has focused on residential, institutional, and commercial project types. In independent practice, Claudia presently is collaborating with a AH Design (www.ahdzmdesign.com), a California-based automotive research, development, and design firm.

Their research focuses on the use and adaptation of automotive fabrication technology and materials for architectural and interior design applications.

title: Professor
bio:
From 2011-2019 Professor Kevin Hom served as Dean at The New York City College of Technology (City Tech) School of Design and Technology. Professor Hom is the founder and President of Kevin Hom Architects. His practice is a national design firm with education facility projects throughout the country. Under Professor Hom's leadership, the practice has won numerous awards including the "2008 Firm of the Year" from the Society of American Registered Architects/New York Council. Mr. Hom is recognized as a leader in the advancement of design and better use of spaces at major colleges and university.

In 2017 Professor Hom was elected a Fellow of the American Institute of Architects, “The fellowship designation is the highest honor the AIA can bestow upon a member. Elevation to Fellowship not only recognizes the achievements of architect as an individual but also elevates before the public and the profession those architects who have made significant contributions to architecture and to society,” notes the AIA. In 2020 Prof Hom was named a Fulbright Scholar at the University of Bologna. In 2019 Professor Hom was a visiting Resident Professor at the Polytechnico di Milan and in 2022 he was a Visiting Professor at Technische Universitaet Berlin.

Professor Hom has spoken on the subject of Architectural design/planning design, urban planning, and climate change at numerous Universities and conferences such as the Association of College Unions International (ACUI) and the Society of College University Planners (SCUP). University of Sao Paulo, Brandeis University, Technical University of Berlin, and The City University of London.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Dr. Jihun Kim is a researcher and educator, instructing both undergraduate and graduate students on sustainability, energy flow, and environmental design in seminars, workshops, and design studios. Having earned a Master of Architecture from the University of Michigan, he has practiced as an architect with a focus on sustainability and is currently licensed in the state of New York and LEED-accredited. His academic journey led him to a Ph.D. in Architecture at the University of Pennsylvania, where he received formal training as a building scientist.

His life’s work centers around advancing sustainability through architectural design and building science research, utilizing environmental simulation and modeling. Dr. Kim actively engages with global challenges, addressing issues such as reducing carbon footprints, finding low-carbon solutions, and predicting disease transmission. These endeavors have resulted in impactful publications and contributions to government policies. Notably, recent research collaborations include projects on airflow and its impacts, such as working with Microsoft to eliminate extreme heat in data centers and tracing COVID-19 transmission for effective elimination.

His expertise encompasses advanced environmental simulation, computational fluid dynamics, bioclimatic architectural optimization, environmental system integration, and low-carbon neighborhood design. Recent publications by Dr. Kim include:

"CARBON WAR “Carbon War! Homes Saving the Earth”, KBS, Korean National Television Documentary Chanel, “DocuOn” (2023)
“Environmental Simulation in Facade Design Education with Emerging Criteria” presented at Façade Tectonic Institute Education Forum (2023)
“New York City’s Decarbonization Path, The NYC Local Law 97 Of 2019” for Seoul Metropolitan Government (2023)
“Unbalancing mean radiant temperature and air temperature” in CISBAT, Journal of Physics (2023)
“Integration of raytracing and CFD simulation to assess the impact of UVGI technology on the control of aerosol transmission in an occupied room” presented at IBPSA (2021)
“Integrating analog analysis techniques and building performance simulation in the architectural design process” presented at IBPSA (2019)
“Topography integration to wind downscaling” published in Building and Environment (2017)
“A rapid indoor airflow mapping with two-dimensional computational fluid dynamics” in Passive & Low Energy Architecture Proceeding (2016)
“An urban-conscious rapid wind downscaling model for early design stages”, a part of his PhD Dissertation (2015)
“Design & Build Competition” for U.S. Department of Energy Solar Decathlon (2015)
“Discovery-Performance-Design” presented at IBPSA (2013)
“Daylight Mapping Using Kriging” presented at IBPSA (2013)
“Building form optimization in the early design stage to reduce adverse wind condition-using computational fluid dynamics” presented at IBPSA (2011)

title: Professor
bio:
• Executive Director of the Brooklyn Waterfront Research Center
  • Member of the American Institute of Architects
  • Member of the American Society of Civil Engineers
  • Past President Society of American Registered Architects /NY Chapter
  • Registered Architect in the State of New York
  • Master of Urban Design, City College
  • BArch, City College
  • BS Landscape Architecture

Professor King holds degrees in Architecture and Landscape Architecture and Urban Design, all from the City College of New York. A Brooklyn native who grew up on the shores of Coney Island, Professor King began his career working as an Architect for Davis Brody and Associates. As an Architect, Professor King was assigned to projects early in the design process guiding the development of CADD based documents to the completion of bid documents. Projects include Hudson Tower at Battery Park City, Cornell Biotechnology Center, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, Lincoln Center North Building & Juilliard School, Zeckendorf Towers, Brooklyn Polytech Library at Metrotech, S.U.N.Y. Buffalo Science & Mathematics Facility and Cornell University Primary Teaching Facility and Research and Veterinary Hospital.

A pioneer in the implementation of Computer Aided Design within the profession of Architecture, Professor King opened his own consulting firm CADD Management Consulting in 1991 providing consulting services to Architects, Landscape Architects, Engineers, and Facilities Managers. In recent years in addition to working on Architecture projects Professor King has focused his efforts on several large scale Landscape Architecture projects including Stanford University's' Science and Engineering Quadrangle in Paolo Alto California and Hudson River Park in New York.

Professor King is a scholar and historian who specializes on the early work of John A. Roebling, the engineer of the Brooklyn Bridge. He is particularly interested in how his early ideas evolved and his influence on the development of the 19th century suspension bridge. Since 2015 he has presented annually to the Society of Industrial Archeology on different aspects of Roebling’s work.

He is in demand as a historical consultant and lecturer and has lent his expertise to the D&H Historical Society, the Roebling Museum and the National Parks Service, who maintains the historic site of Roebling’s historic Delaware Aqueduct, the oldest surviving suspension bridge in America and one of only three Roebling bridges remaining – the two others being the Cincinnati-Covington Bridge and the Brooklyn Bridge.

He continues to publish journal articles on the topic and is currently completing his book titled, “Roebling Before the Brooklyn Bridge” — to be published by ORO editions.

In 2024 Professor King took over the leadership of the Brooklyn Waterfront Research Center (BWRC) as the new executive director. Institutionally affiliated with CityTech, the BWRC supports a 3-part mission that includes Education, Research and Public Events that focus on the Brooklyn Waterfront.

title: Associate Professor
bio:

MArch, Yale University
Registered Architect in the State of New York

Anne Leonhardt has a M.ARCH. from the Yale School of Architecture, and a M.A. and B.A. with Honors in History and Urban Planning from St. John's College, Cambridge University. Her research, teaching, and design practice focus on the material and environmental interfaces between architectural design, form, and tectonics. Areas of expertise include associative computational design, building performance analysis, information modeling systems, fabrication, and sustainable materials and energy. She is director of digital fabrication for the department.

She has coordinated a number of New York State Perkins grants (Integrating Emerging Technologies for Collaborative Learning: Performative Building Analysis, Parametric Modeling, and Building Information Modeling Systems) that focus on cross disciplinary integration of tools for building performance analysis and parametric and building information modeling in the School of Technology and Design's programs. She is also a recipient of a PSC-CUNY research award to further research in this area.

Leonhardt co-launched the School of Technology and Design's Emerge Lecture series, which focuses on an examination of recent technologies and thinking in the interstitial spaces between design and engineering. Professor Leonhardt edited and contributed to a book published last year, South Street Seaport: Re-Envisioning the Urban Edge, a Visual and Written Exploration, on the ideas raised in the AIA New York International Biennial competition of the same name. The publication includes essays by renowned academics, Michael Sorkin and Anne Buttenweiser. Her work has also been published in the journal, Retrospecta. and exhibited at the Corcoran Museum of Art in Washington, DC. She has a background in research on urbanism and sustainable development from several years of work with the U.N. and World Bank.

She heads a design-build consulting practice focusing on sustainable design, materials, fabrication, and computation, an area in which she has worked for the past decade.

title: Lecturer
bio: Professor M' Bourokounda is currently a doctoral student in architecture at Columbia's GSAPP where she is researching late 19th and early 20th century Atlantic and Caribbean history with a focus on the French West Indies. Her research interests concern the intersection of built space and colonial ecologies in the Americas at the end of the 19th century and the intersection of the environment, social and economic structures and built space. Professor M' Bourokounda received a Bachelor in Arts in Architecture from Ball State University and a Master of Architecture from Princeton University’s School of Architecture.

title: Assistant Professor

Professor Eugene Seungho Park is an architect, designer, and educator based in New York City. He is the founding principal of STUDIO KYSH—, an interdisciplinary architecture studio established in 2019, where he leads a diverse portfolio of residential and commercial renovation projects across the NYC metropolitan area and Seoul, Korea. His practice has earned international recognition through notable awards, such as the winning masterplan for the Korea Pavilion at Expo 2025 in Osaka and a second-place award for the Jeonju Railway Station International Competition.

In addition to his architectural practice, Eugene serves as a senior advisor to HanmiGlobal, focusing on advancing construction management strategies and fostering industry-wide collaborations. His research interests extend to broader areas of sustainability, including Design for Disassembly (DfD), Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA), mass timber, prefab and modular construction, and adaptive reuse.

His commitment to academia is further demonstrated through independent projects, such as the "Architecture of Insecurity" (2021) exhibition at SPACE776 New York, funded by a research grant from the Korean Government. As an educator, he has delivered lectures and workshops at various institutions around the world including École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Parsons School of Design, University of Cincinnati, and Hongik University.

Before establishing his practice, Eugene played a key role in multiple civic and cultural projects during his tenure at Adjaye Associates and MIT Urban Risk Lab, with major contributions to the Studio Museum in Harlem in New York City.

title: Professor
bio:
• BArch – Cornell University
  • PhD – Architectural History, Columbia University
  • Member of the American Institute of Architects
  • Registered Architect – New York

Professor Smith’s practice, scholarship, and teaching focus on construction technologies, preservation, and architectural history. Projects, publications, and presentations have included the use of ground penetrating radar (GPR) for the investigation of historic masonry structures, monitoring techniques for timber frame construction, analysis of masonry coatings, historic resource surveys and the development of local preservation law, cultural landscapes, vernacular buildings of the colonial Americas, mid-century modern low-rise housing, and the role of architectural history in design education. These projects have been published and presented for the journals and conferences of the Society of Architectural Historians, the Vernacular Architecture Forum, the Association for Preservation Technology International, and the South Carolina Historical Magazine.

Grant activities include: Project Director of STEM Success Collaborative, funded by a Developing Hispanic Serving Institutions grant from the US Department of Education (2021-2026), PD of the National Science Foundation Fuse Lab: Collaborative Education for Tomorrow’s Technology in Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (2011-2015), Assistant PD of Along the Shore: Changing and Preserving the Landmarks of Brooklyn’s Industrial Waterfront from the National Endowment for the Humanities, and CoPI on the Living Laboratory: Redesigning General Education for a 21st-Century College of Technology from the US Department of Education.

Professor Smith is a former chair of the Department of Architectural Technology (2010-2015), was Faculty Co-Chair of the college Middle States self-study and accreditation (2016-2018), and currently serves as Co-Director of City Tech’s Faculty Commons.

Prior to joining City Tech in 2007, Professor Smith was an Associate with the architectural preservation firm of Walter Sedovic Architects; Project Architect for commercial, retail, and residential projects with Buttrick White & Burtis; and an adjunct assistant professor at Marymount College (Fordham University) teaching history of interiors and historic preservation.

title: Associate Professor
bio:

An actively practicing architect, Sanjive has twenty-five years of professional and field experience, working for Pei Cobb Freed & Partners and then Davis Brody Bond Architects. His work under J. Max Bond included research institutes, performing arts centers, and master planning projects for the Department of State Overseas Building Operations. Sanjive’s studio, established in 2005 in Brooklyn, is engaged in residential and commercial architecture and interiors. He currently serves on the Board of Directors at the Architectural League of New York.

Sanjive’s role as an educator and department chair has evolved into an inquiry of how a design student’s good intentions are supplanted by economic forces that bend their will and erode optimistic agendas. This process sacrifices a designers most radical potential. Public design programs function as incubators for positive action on behalf of the displaced and underserved. Cultivating a designers agency must be the singular goal of design education.

title: Associate Professor/B.ARCH Co-Director
bio:
• M.Arch, Columbia GSAPP
  • B.A. in Architecture, Yale University
  • Registered Architect in the State of New York
  • Member, American Institute of Architects
  • USGBC Member, LEED AP BD+C
  • Passive House Institute U.S. Certified Consultant, CPHC

Professor Yang is the founding principal of Habitat Workshop, an award-winning architecture and urban design practice based in Brooklyn, NY. Habitat Workshop creates spaces, objects, and interactions that activate human connections, build resiliency, and reveal the intrinsic value of a place. With projects ranging from arts and civic spaces to homes and interiors, the practice promotes design as an accessible framework for positive changes by exploring the extraordinary potential in the ordinary.

Recent awards and honors include AN Best of Design, NYCxDESIGN Awards, Forge Prize Finalist, Interior Design’s Best in Design, and Women in Design. Her work has been featured in the 2023 Venice Biennale at the European Cultural Center and Mannheim 2023 BUGA. Her public art projects have been featured at Times Square and BKYN Designs.

Professor Yang is a fellow at the Urban Design Forum and completed residencies at the Institute for Public Architecture and Art Omi: Architecture. As the Stewardson Keefe LeBrun Grant and SOM Prize recipient, her research explores comparative studies on urban infrastructure and housing models across continents.

Before founding Habitat Workshop, Professor Yang has worked at SOM, BKSK, and 1100: Architect, working on a wide array of transportation, cultural, public, and residential projects. She is an active collaborator with Design Advocates and has served on the publications committee at the Center for Architecture.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
BArch and MPS Design Management, Pratt Institute
Registered Architect, NY

Professor Zagaroli holds a bachelor of architecture and a master of professional studies in design management from Pratt Institute. Born, raised and educated in Brooklyn, he has provided technical assistance for hundreds of units of rehabilitated housing, several community facility buildings and countless feasibility analyses for not-for-profit organizations in developing neighborhoods throughout the five boroughs.

Working recently with Lynn Gernert Architects where his detailing, design and construction knowledge was applied to sensitive rejuvenations of several urban and rural homes and townhouses. He is currently designing a community center for the Federation of Italian American Organizations, which will be the home of the first Italian American Community Center in New York City.

title: Professor
bio:
Mary Ann Biehl is an Associate Professor and the chair of the Advertising Design & Graphic Arts Department at New York City College of Technlogy, CUNY.

Prof Biehl holds a Master of Science degree from Pratt Institute and a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree from St. John's University. She has also taught design courses at Southampton College, Long Island University and St. John's University.

Prof. Biehl teaches courses in Typography, Visual Communications, Corporate Identity, and Information and Exhibtion Design.

She is the curriculum and course coordinator for both the Typography curriculum and Visual Communication courses. In addition, Prof. Biehl is the Faculty Advisor for the Department's student Image Makers Club as well as the student scholarship selection committee.

Along with her responsibities at City Tech, Prof. Biehl maintains her professional design practice, which focuses on corporate identity design. Some of her clients include Adecco International, Olsten Corporation, iPEC Coaching, and Professionals for Non-Profits.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Lloyd Carr is a designer and producer in online (interactive/internet) and offline (print) graphic communications media. His focus is on issues of science, technology, engineering and mathematics outcomes. He is also concerned with efficiency, effectiveness, sustainability, social interaction and education.

Professor Carr has combined these topics to help students understand how their interests can be applied to identify problems and find solutions with communication design and management challenges.

Lloyd Carr is an Associate Professor at City Tech (CUNY) since 1998. Professor Carr has a Master of Arts in Journalism & Communications (1972) from the University of Florida and a Bachelor of Science in Advertising (1971), also from the University of Florida. He has been certified in "preflight" from Markzware; and holds certificates in digital imaging prepress and digital presswork from Xerox. Professor Carr continues to be active in the communications industry, consulting to media, output and imaging companies.

Prior to his arrival at City Tech, Professor Carr worked for Applied Graphics Technologies (AGT) where he managed computer-to-plate (CTP) workflows, established digital preflight procedures, and developed digital archiving/digital asset management systems for advertising and publishing. Professor Carr's current research is in practical, applied research to develop education and management of color in all offline (print) and online (smartphone/tablet/webpage) graphic media.

Professor Carr's articles on color have been published in multiple Association of Graphic Communications Buyers Guides. He has presented at multiple sessions of Graph Expos and Print Expos in Chicago during his tenure at City Tech.

Professor Carr has been a member of the Committee for Graphic Arts Technologies Standards (CGATS), with the purpose of developing American National Standards, since 1999.

title: Professor
bio:
Brooklyn-based Douglas Davis enjoys being one of the variety of voices needed in front of and behind the concept. His approach to creativity combines right-brained creative problem solving with left-brained strategic thinking. Douglas’ integrated point of view has enabled his natural evolution from designer to strategist, author, and professor. He has found an international audience interested in his approach to blurring the lines between advertising, design, and business education. Douglas enjoys interacting with creative people and regularly presents at industry conferences including HOW Design Live, RGD Design Thinkers, and The One Club Educators Summit.

In 2016, Douglas wrote Creative Strategy and the Business of Design, a title translated into Mandarin and released in 2020 by Beijing Normal University. He is a former co-chair of AIGA’s National Diversity and Inclusion Taskforce and regularly contributes to the business of design discourse in Printmag.com, Applied Arts, and The European Business Review. Douglas founded The Davis Group LLC in 2011 and continues to offer strategic solutions to client branding, digital, and design problems. In addition to client work, Douglas leverages his professional experience to inspire high school, undergraduate, and graduate students. As the longest-serving member on the 4As High School Advisory Board, his experience was translated into the four-year curriculum at New York City’s High School for Innovation in Advertising and Media (iAM). Following the launch, Douglas contributed as an education consultant for the Manhattan Early College School for Advertising (MECA) launch.

Douglas is an Emmy Award-winning strategist who serves on the advisory boards of the Poster House Museum CMYK council, The Type Director’s Club, The University of Oregon’s Masters in Advertising and Brand Responsibility, and City College’s Masters in Branding and Integrated Communications. He is former Chair of the B.F.A. in Communication Design program at New York City College of Technology in Brooklyn and holds a B.A. in Graphic Design from Hampton University, an M.S. in Communications Design from Pratt Institute, and an M.S. in Integrated Marketing from New York University. Creative Strategist, Educator & Author, who depends on what day.

title: Chair
bio:
George Garrastegui, Jr. is a design educator and creative consultant in New York City. He has a background in publishing, marketing, and strategy, which has allowed him to craft solutions for brands such as Esquire, Ford, Cadillac, and Popular Mechanics. When not teaching strategic problem-solving and process at CUNY’s New York City College of Technology (City Tech), George works to create industry connections and build a pipeline from school to career. He is fueled by the pursuit of uncovering ways to give emerging designers access and opportunities as a member of both the AIGA DEI initiative and 100 Roses from Concrete.

In 2017 George started the award-winning Works in Process podcast that documents the working styles of creative individuals. The podcast reframes the idea that creativity is a solitary endeavor— guests share how their journeys are by-products of determination and a systematic approach to solving problems. In 2021, George was asked to Chair and Moderate the 2021 AIGA Design + Business conference and “Take a deep dive into the creative process to discuss 12 notable, impactful, and innovative projects from the teams that created them.” Over the years, he’s learned that there’s no one way to be a creative, but endless possibilities fueled by passion, purpose, and process.

George has earned both his AAS in Illustration and his BFA in Graphic Design from New York’s Fashion Institute of Technology and his MFA in Graphic Design from the Savannah College of Art + Design.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Anita Giraldo is an Assistant Professor in the Communication Design Department at New York City College of Technology. Professor Giraldo received her MFA from the School of Visual Arts and her BFA from the Cooper Union.

Before coming to City Tech as a full-time professor, Professor Giraldo taught image management at the International Center for Photography. She has worked in the production management environment for Time Out New York, LTB Media, Quad Graphics, Ruder Finn PRP, Sesame Street and Meigher Communications. She operated her own commercial photography studio during which time she photographed numerous national ad campaigns, catalogs and editorial stories.

In 2007 she was commissioned to document the industrial architecture of Columbia County by the Columbia County Historical Society, resulting in an exhibition at the Columbia County Museum in Kinderhook, NY. In 2005 she won an artist fellowship from the Puffin Foundation to travel to the US Gulf Coast to photograph the shipbuilding industry in the wake of Hurricane Katrina. She also won a grant from the National Endowment for the Arts and The New York State Council for the Arts for her photo-documentary work.

Her fine art work showed in the US and throughout Europe. Currently touring, an interactive sensory installation, Steel, Ice & Stone premiered at the ArtLab Trenton in 2013 and the conceptual art venue, The Gowanus Ballroom in June 2014. See My Voice, a multimedia interactive installation, was exhibited in Ohio and Amsterdam in 1996, Cologne (1998) and in Brooklyn (2009) in public venues.

title: Professor
bio:
Maria Giuliani is an Associate Professor in the Department of Communication Design at New York City College of Technology. She has been part of the City Tech faculty since 1997. In addition, she has taught at Pratt Institute, were she also earned an MS in Communication Design. Maria also holds a BA in Commercial Art from the American College for Applied Arts, and a Certificate in Illustration from the New York Botanical Garden.

Since 2002 she has been the coordinator of the department's Grace Gallery.

She has worked in publishing, specializing in book design. Her book cover designs and posters have won local and national awards. She currently designs and illustrates for various organizations and businesses, and her work has been exhibited in various city art spaces.

Affiliations

Type Directors Club, member

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Tanya Goetz is an Assistant Professor in the Communication Design Department of New York City College of Technology. A 1987 graduate from the University of Connecticut with a B.A. in Economics and Journalism, she earned a MA from Hunter College in 2001.

Prior to joining NYCCT’s faculty in 2003, Professor Goetz worked in publishing for over 16 years at various trade and consumer publications. As prepress manager for Scientific American, she managed the magazine’s transition to computer-to-plate (CTP), making it the nation’s first magazine to eliminate film in its production processes. She also helped establish Scientific American's first digital archive that allowed readers to access articles in PDF format from prior years. In 1998, she became Quality & Technology manager for U.S. News & World Report, where she developed the magazine’s digital ad specifications, and coordinated the establishment of an in-house prepress facility. While at U.S. News, she also worked with the production staffs of Fast Company and the Atlantic Monthly to transition those publications to digital advertising and CTP workflows.

Working with groups such as the DDAP (Digital Distribution for Advertising in Production) she promoted the adoption of standardized ad specifications. In recognition of these efforts, she was named a member of the “Folio 40,” a listing of publishing’s 40 most influential people in 2001. Professor Goetz continues to support industry efforts to streamline workflows. She is a member of the Adveritsing Production Club (APC), the American Institute of Graphic Arts (AIGA) and of the American Print History Association (APHA). She is particularly interested in color management across devices and the setting of industry-wide standards for digital photography. Professor Goetz hopes to share with her students the endless fascination of managing color in multiple color spaces--CMYK, RGB, LAB, etc.-- in a world where no two individuals see color the same way.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
M. Genevieve Hitchings is an Associate Professor in the Communication Design Department at New York City College of Technology. She is Principal designer of ARTORIUM, a design studio producing projects that concentrate on information design and illustration. She considers her work a form of art journalism, communicating the essentials of carefully researched information quickly and clearly as a visualized narrative. She has been responsible for project management, art direction, design, and illustration in the development of a wide range of multimedia projects. She has worked as a contract artist for scientists at several research organizations. Her clients include the American Museum of Natural History, the NYC Department of Parks and Recreation, and the Mid-Atlantic Regional Seed Bank (MARS-B).

Her work has been featured in several exhibitions, including the Guild of Natural Science Illustrators (GNSI), the Art Gallery of the American Association for the Advancement of Science in Washington, D.C., and the New York State Museum in Albany’s Focus On Nature exhibit at the Roberson Museum and Science Center in Binghamton, NY. She has received recognition from American Illustration (AI-AP). She regularly presents her research at design conferences including the American Institute of Graphic Arts (AIGA), the College Art Association (CAA), and Foundations in Art: Theory and Education (FATE). She holds a Master of Fine Arts degree from the Fashion Institute of Technology and a Bachelor of Arts degree from Hampshire College.

title: Lecturer
bio:
Lyubava Kroll (she/her/hers), MDes, is a multidisciplinary visual communications creative. Her research interests include interdisciplinary learning and participatory design as methods to promote social awareness. She has previously worked as a design consultant for the Government of Alberta (Canada), University of Alberta (Canada), National Research Council of Canada, Sustainable Waterloo Region (Canada), World Animal Protection (USA), National Dance Institute (USA), and National Association of City Transportation Officials (USA).

Before joining CUNY's New York City College of Technology as a Lecturer in 2023, Lyubava led global brand and visual communications at the United Nations Global Compact based in the New York headquarters. Alongside her professional industry roles, she has shared her expertise through courses at institutions including Lehigh University, Conestoga College Institute of Technology, University of Waterloo, University of Alberta, and Digital Arts College of Edmonton.

Lyubava specializes in branding, creative direction, design strategy, and UX. Her personal artistic practice includes illustration and painting, where she explores the topics of sustainability and topophilia. She has earned multiple design awards, and her artwork has been showcased in both juried and non-juried exhibitions throughout the USA and Canada.

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
With a foundation rooted in independent exploration, my journey into the realm of art commenced with a self directed study of photography and the nuanced world of image production, where I initially played the role of a photo assistant. Captivated by the narrative potential of images, I became fascinated by their ability to challenge viewers, prompting introspection and reshaping perceptions of self and the world.

This passion led me to the prestigious Art Center College of Design in Pasadena, California, where I earned my B.F.A. in Photography. Here, I delved into the essence of concept development, the transformative power of research, and the disciplined mastery of technical skills to breathe life into my artistic vision. The educational odyssey continued at Pratt Institute in Brooklyn, where I pursued my M.F.A. and embarked on a transition from analog to the dynamic realm of digital image making.

During my M.F.A. journey, I explored digital photography and ventured into the world of Photoshop and motion graphics, unveiling the possibilities of time based digital image creation. The culmination of this work manifested in my thesis show, a fusion of large format photography and prints with a digital video piece. This video portrayed the nuances of time, beauty, and decay, weaving individual journeys through urban landscapes and incorporating images of insects and type elements as archival records.

Fueling my artistic fervor, my global travels provided opportunities to engage with diverse cultures, and spending summers working in Paris proved to be an especially enriching experience. Beyond photography, I have contributed digital visual elements to l ive dance and music performances, crafted short films blending film imagery with digital components, and infused commercial work with a tension between the appealing and disturbing.

Participating in the School of Visual Arts Residency Program in Sculpture and New Media, I ventured into creating dystopian 3D images exploring the theme of insanity. The culmination of this endeavor led to my selection as a highlighted artist in a Venezue lan television feature on the program’s exhibition, as well as recognition in SVA's own media promotions.

Currently, as a tenured assistant professor at New York City College of Technology, I continue to draw inspiration from the ever evolving interplay between analog and digital mediums, weaving a tapestry of art that challenges, captivates, and reflects the complexity of the human experience.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
John McVicker is an Associate Professor of Advertising Design in the Communication Design Department at New York City College of Technology. Professor McVicker received his master's in advertising design from The City College of New York (CUNY) and his bachelor's degree from the School of Visual Arts.

Professor McVicker began his career at McCann-Erickson Worldwide (part of Interpublic).

In addition to McCann, Professor McVicker's ad agency experience includes Dancer, Fitzgerald, Sample (now Saatchi & Saatchi) where he rose to the rank of vice president. In 1991, he started his own company, Ad+Plus Concept & Design Inc. Some of his major account experience includes: Coke, BMW, New York Racing Association (NYRA), Toyota, Schick, Seagrams, Procter & Gambel (P&G), General Mills, Japan Airlines (JAL) and Mead Papers.

In addition to art direction, Professor McVicker is a full TV producer and has produced many national commercials for: Duracell, General Mills, P&G and Toyota. His TV work has been cited in Advertising Age's 100 Best TV spots. He has won just about every major advertising award, including a Clio, a gold Effie, numerous Art Directors Club and Type Directors Club awards plus 2 gold ADDYs. The Museum of Modern Art (MOMA) recognized Professor McVicker's work with three of his pieces in their permanent graphic design collection.

Professor McVicker teaches concept courses at both the associate and baccalaureate levels. Specifically ADV2300, 2400, 3500, 3600 advertising campaign development courses. He is currently writing a book on the process of concept advertising. His ADV4701 Design Team course takes on many real world assignments such as designing an ad campaign for the Long island Hospital's Rape Crisis Intervention Center. From 2000 to 2007, he chaired the department's seminar series bringing in over 40 top industry professionals to the college. Distinguished speakers included NY Art Director's Hall of Famers: George Lois, Pushpin Studio co-founder Seymour Chwast, Roy Grace, Jay Maisel, Sal DeVito, BBDO Phil Dusenberry's post 9/11 NYC campaign team and interactive pioneer Edwin Schlossberg - just to name a few.

Prof. McVicker was responsible for initially connecting with the One Club for Art & Copy.

This connection has resulted in annual student scholarships, shows and internships. In 2007, after his students participated in the first One Club International Student Show, Prof. McVicker was invited to Beijing, China to teach at the Beijing Fashion Institute of Technology. In appreciation, he was awarded the rank of Distinguished Visiting Professor. Professor McVicker has written a course outline for a new copywriting course for advertising. He has also encouraged the department to create a bullpen, where important presentation skills could be learned by students. Professor McVicker believes that students who understand both concept and technology - will be the leaders in tomorrow's multi-channel advertising world.

title: Professor
bio:
Robin Michals is a photographer whose focus since 2021 has been on dance and performance. Recent clients have included the American Guild Dance, Artichoke Dance, the Center for Performance Research, Creative Performances, Downtown Brooklyn Partnership, the International Human Rights Arts Festival and the Queensboro Dance Festival among others. Before the pandemic, for over 12 years, her work documented environmental issues. Her series Our Neighborhood juxtaposes sites of residential life in cities and towns across the US with the infrastructure of the fossil fuel industries. This work was exhibited at St. Francis University in Philadelphia, the Marshall J. Gardener Center for the Arts in Gary, Indiana and as part of the 8th Edition of THE FENCE in 2019-2020. The series was selected for Critical Mass Top 50 in 2019 and in 2020, it was one of eight winners of the 7th Tokyo International Photography Competition.

Before joining the Communication Design Department at New York City College of Technology, for 14 years, she worked as an art director and designer for numerous print and online communications. She designed new and special interest publications for TV Guide, Ladies Home Journal, Weight Watchers, and American Lawyer Media. She was the Senior Designer of FOX Sports Online from 1996-1998. She designed the first online presence for The New Yorker magazine as well as CondeNast's Lucky Magazine.

She holds a BA from Barnard College and an MFA from Columbia University.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Eli Neugeboren is an Assistant Professor specializing in digital imaging technology in the Communication Design Department at New York City College of Technology. Professor Neugeboren holds a Masters of Fine Arts degree from University of California, Santa Barbara, and a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Painting from Ohio University.

Professor Neugeboren is a retoucher, illustrator, designer, and artist who has worked in the digital imaging field for the past 10 years, and in the creative and design world since 1997. He was the first in-house digital imaging specialist at Spin magazine, where he developed the magazine's workflow and was responsible for the retouching, coloring correction and overall quality of every image in the publication for nearly 4 years. Professor Neugeboren has also worked as a graphic designer in the American Museum of Natural History's exhibition department and was a Teaching Artist for the Museum of Modern Art and Lincoln Center Institute. He continues his work in all of these specialties as a freelancer.

In 2003 Professor Neugeboren traveled to the Venice Biennale, where he was a resident artist in Marko Peljhan's Makrolab. Makrolab is concerned with work in three areas: the electromagnetic spectrum, migration, and meteorology. Participants work on their own projects as well as collaborative works with other resident artists.

Clients Served: Ideo, Publicis, Clarins, Redken, Hennessy, Maybelline, Sony Music, Smart Tuition, Ecko Unltd, Intel, People Magazine, Little Brown & Co., W, Wallpaper, Surface, Glamour, Spin Magazine, Rolling Stone Magazine, Peter Yang, David LaChapelle, Nigel Barker, Atumn De Wilde, Terry Richardson, Cass Bird, Mark Mann, Ben Watts.

title: Professor
bio:
As an artist, designer, and educator, Professor Spevack uses interactive and participatory practices to explore how interactions with nature, simulated and real, can help to rekindle a sense of awe and a deeper connectedness to the natural world.

A Professor in the Communication Design Department, she has served as OpenLab Co-Director since 2011, under the college’s Title V individual development grant, “A Living Laboratory” (2011-2016) and as part of related collaborative grants including: “Learning in the Public Square” Digital Humanities Implementation NEH Grant with the CUNY Graduate Center, Co-Director - Design (2016-2018); “Digital Pathways” Title III HSI-STEM with BMCC, Development Lead (2016-2021); and “Opening Gateways” Title V Cooperative Arrangement Grant, WeBWorK Integration Co-Director (2015-2019).

In addition to directing the design and development of City Tech’s OpenLab and the publicly released, CBOX OpenLab, Prof. Spevack has helped to develop the university’s first Bachelors of Fine Arts in Communication Design, a Bachelors Degree in Emerging Media, a certificate in Interactive Media, and currently in progress, a Perkins-funded Collaboratory for faculty and student research in immersive media. She has taught courses in and served as course coordinator for web design, interactive media, animation, design foundations, and design theory.

With over 20 years experience as a designer, she has contributed to the development of a variety of web-based and interactive media, including those for Sesame Workshop and PBS Kids. As an artist, she is the recipient of numerous grants, fellowships, and residencies and has exhibited her work nationally and internationally.

Portfolio / Research: JennaSpevack.com

Teaching: ProfSpevack.com

title: Professor
bio:
Dan Wong is Professor of Web Design in the Communication Design Department at New York City College of Technology, CUNY. Professor Wong holds a Masters of Fine Art degree from Cranbrook Academy of Art, a four-year AOCA degree from the Ontario College of Art and Design and a Bachelor of Science from the University of Toronto.

Since 1999 Professor Wong has been working in the field of Medical Communications. He has worked as creative director of design and marketing in educational publishing, pharmaceutical marketing, and continuing medical education (CME). He has launched corporate products, directed design services, and created technology solutions for both established global companies and start-ups.

Professor Wong has combined his interests in science, education, communications, business, technology and the arts to bring an understanding to students whose interests span a variety of topics.

Clients served: Pfizer, GlaxoSmithKline, Boehringer Ingelheim, Altana, Bristol-Myers Squibb, Novartis, Abbott, Elsevier, MediMedia USA, Inc, Dowden Health Media, Inc. and others.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Professor Seymour Blank earned his master's in electrical engineering from Polytechnic University in 1968 and his PhD in physiology from Cornell University in 1986. Before joining the CET/EMT department at City Tech, he was a faculty member of NY Hospital-Cornell University Medical Center (New York, NY). Professor Blank's research activity has been related to the noninvasive analysis of the cardiovascular system. He has developed a new method for measuring blood pressure (using the wideband external blood pressure measurement pulse) and has a patent entitled "Wideband External Pulse Cardiac Monitor." His present research interest is the analysis of the physical properties of the cardiovascular system.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Dr. Aparicio Carranza earned his PhD degree in Electrical Engineering from The Graduate School and University Center - CUNY; BSEE (summa cum laude) & MSEE from The City College of New York - CUNY and his AAS (summa cum laude) in Electronics Circuits and Systems from Technical Career Institutes of NY. He joined the Computer Engineering Technology Department of the The New York City College of Technology as full time faculty on fall 2000. Before becoming a full time, he was an adjunct faculty for four years at the same department. For several years he worked as an Engineer - Scientist at the Development Division of IBM Corp. (RS6000 parallel computers; and S/390 mainframe computers) in Poughkeepsie, NY. He teaches Analog Electronics, Digital Electronics, Programming Languages (MATLAB, C, C++, Java, etc.), Engineering Analysis, Data Communications, Engineering Design and other related courses.

title: Associate Professor
bio:

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Dr. Benito (Ben) Mendoza works at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, education, and real-world applications. His research focuses on applied AI systems, including machine learning, multi-agent systems, swarm intelligence, and knowledge-based architectures, with an emphasis on socially responsive AI and how these technologies function in complex social settings.

He leads an NSF-funded project that integrates cultural, linguistic, and infrastructure factors into AI-powered information systems to help people access food-security services. His team studies how demographic and local data affect communication and engagement, and how AI can guide better outreach to underserved communities.

In parallel, Dr. Mendoza is actively involved in advancing AI education, career readiness, and workforce development. He serves on City Tech’s AI Task Force and is the Founder and Director of the City Tech TC2 Hub Microcredentials Program, which supports flexible training, promotes professional certifications and microcredentials, and enables learners to document and communicate verified competencies through digital badges. As an NAIRR AI Education Fellow at the Computer Research Association, supported by NSF, he participates in national conversations on AI access, AI literacy, and research infrastructure in higher education.

Before joining City Tech in 2011, Dr. Mendoza was a Postdoctoral Research Engineer at ExxonMobil Research & Engineering. He has also worked as a software engineer and project manager in government, education, and entertainment. In 2018, he completed a Faculty Residency at Google. These experiences shape his research and teaching today.

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Professor Morton is a Licensed Professional Engineer and his areas of endeavor include Arduino, Raspberry Pi, Motorola Launchpad, Intel 8051, propeller and Intel Galileo Microcontroller systems, LabView systems, Digital controls, computer systems, electronics, programming, MATLAB (a scientific and engineering software tool); Industrial controls, Motors, Op Amps, Pneumatics /Hydraulics, Relays(electromechanical and Solid State), Robotics, Programmable Logic Controllers(PLC), Automation, clean room technology, the design, development and manufacture/installation of DVD, CD, digital audio, MPEG2 (encoding technology) components and systems; and the design, development and manufacture of the electronic/magnetic ballasts and compact fluorescent lamps that comprise the compact fluorescent lamp. Ed Morton led the team that developed one of the first commercially available CFL's (from conception to prototype construction to manufacture). The Westinghouse "ECON NOVA", the before mentioned CFL (Compact Fluorescent Lamp), is on display at the Smithsonian Institute museum, Washington, D.C.

He has Sensor technology, interface circuit experience, Thyristors, ASICs, Switch mode power supplies, Analog /Digital Electronics, Industrial controls, Injection molding, vacuum metallization, lacquer coating experience, "Vision" Computer Systems, SPC, ISO 9000, Oracle, Solid state, continuous Gas laser technology, Optics, Electro-optics, Photoresist technology, Barcodes and High Rise Storage Technology experience. He developed Flash lamp and pulse Laser circuit technology. He also has Stepper Motor, DC motor, asynchronous /synchronous motor systems, UL, FCC and NEMA experience.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
José M. Reyes Álamo did his undergraduate studies in Computer Science at the University of Puerto Rico at Bayamón. After graduation he worked in the industry but his strong passion for education and research brought him back to school a year later. He went to Iowa State University (ISU) to pursue his Ph.D. in Computer Science. During his time at ISU he worked in the Smart Home Lab researching topics in Software Engineering, Smart Homes, Pervasive Computing, Formal Methods, and Wireless Sensors. He published several papers and completed his dissertation entitled "A framework for safe composition of heterogeneous SOA services in a pervasive computing environment with resource constraints". In ISU he was also involved in several other activities like organizing the GMAP Symposium, participating in student organizations, and working as research assistant. After graduation he worked for a trading software company in New York City but once again his love for academics brought him back, this time as a professor in Computer Engineering Technology, to the CUNY - New York City College of Technology.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Dr. Chen Xu joined the CET department at City Tech as an Assistant Professor in 2015. Prof. Xu received her Ph.D. degree in Biomedical Engineering from the University of Connecticut. She received her master’s degrees in biomedical engineering and applied physics from the University of Connecticut and Northwestern Polytechnic University of China, respectively. Prior to joining the CET Department, she worked as a Postdoctoral Fellow in the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department at the University of Connecticut, and she also worked as the adjunct professor at the Biomedical Engineering Department at the same time. Prof. Xu’s research areas of interest are in biomedical sensors and instrumentations, image processing, signal processing, and non-invasive medical test.

title: Lecturer
bio:
Professor Archibald received her M.S. degree from City College and professional certificate in Computer Technology from New York University.

She has worked in Fortune 500 companies as a Database Administrator and Trainer. In addition, she has done software training for New York City Agencies. Her interest is in Web Design, Information Technology, and various software applications.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Dr. Bellehsen brings to City Tech a distinguished record in both academia and industry. He received a bachelor's and master's degrees from the University of Paris and his Ph.D. from Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences at NYU.

Dr. Bellehsen's experience in industry includes work with Grumman Aerospace Corporation and Bell Communications Research. His work at Harris Corporation won a second prize at the AUTOTESTCON conference.

Dr. Bellehsen is conversant with a variety of computer languages and fluent in French, Hebrew and Arabic.

title: Professor
bio:
Dr. Candido Cabo received his degree in Electrical Engineering from Universidad Politecnica de Madrid (Spain) and his Ph.D. in Biomedical Engineering from Duke University (Durham, North Carolina). Before joining City Tech, he was a postdoctoral fellow at the SUNY Health Sciences Center at Syracuse, and a research scientist at Columbia University.

He brings to City Tech many years of experience in different areas of scientific computing (programming languages, databases, numerical analysis, visualization) and research. His current research interest is the use of computer simulation to understand complex biological systems.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Dr. Yu-Wen Chen received her Ph.D. degree in Computer Engineering from Iowa State University, M.S. degree in Electrical Engineering from Columbia University, and B.S. degree in Communication Engineering from National Central University in Taiwan.

Dr. Chen has interdisciplinary research background including the cloud-based energy management, demand response, electric vehicle charging scheduling, mobile communication, fairness, and peer-to-peer networking. Her research interests span a range of topics in smart grid, large-scale data analysis, cloud computing, optimization, communication networking, security, and Internet of Thing.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Dr. Elena Filatova received BS in Applied Mathematics from Moscow State University, MS in Computational Linguistics from the University of Southern California, and PhD in Computer Science from Columbia University.

Her research focuses on Natural Language Processing theory and applications.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Dr. Janusz Kusyk received BS and MA degrees from Brooklyn College of the City University of New York. He was awarded PhD degree in Computer Science at the Graduate Center, CUNY in 2012. Prior to joining City Tech, he was a Patent Examiner in US Patent and Trademark Office, where he analyzed and evaluated patent applications in areas of information security, cryptography, and communication networks.

His interests include applications of game theory and biologically inspired algorithms to communication networks and security, especially with applications to MANETs, sensor networks, and distributed robotics tasks.

title: Professor
bio:
Professor X. Li received his Ph.D. from the Graduate Center of CUNY. Having worked for five years as a security specialist in the IT industry before coming to City Tech, Professor Li is now building the information security laboratory which is supported by DOD. Professor Li is also a faculty member of Ph.D. programs in Computer Science and Physics at the CUNY Graduate Center, instructing doctoral candidates.

In fall 2004 and spring 2005, he received a CUNY Salute to Scholars Award, honoring outstanding scholarly achievements and contributions to the creation and transmittal of knowledge. Dr. Li's research includes information security, quantum information and physics. His research is supported by NSF and DOD.

title: Chair
bio: Dr. Milonas has over 11 years experience in database administration, management and organizational training. Dr. Milonas has been teaching in the Computer Systems Technology Department, New York City Technical College since 1997. She has a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science and English Literature from Fordham University, a Masters of Science in Information Systems from New York University and a Ph.D. from Long Island University. Her research interests focus on Knowledge Organization (KO) particularly in the result pages of Web Search Engines. Dr. Milonas has several publications related to KO and search engines and hopes to continue publishing.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Dr. Douglas Moody has been with the CityTech since 2001, bringing years of industry experience to the computer science. During his industry career, Prof. Moody has worked at several top IT companies, including IBM, as well as for public sector entities, such as the City of New York.
His work has always centered on application development, particularly in the public sector.  

He has a M.B.A in information science from Pace University and a Ph.D. in computer science, from the CUNY Graduate Center.

His academic research has focused on developing platforms teaching computational thinking and integrating Artificial Intelligence capabilities into classroom exercises.

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Professor Oudjehane received his bachelor's degree from Polytechnic University of Algeria and his master's degree from Rice University. He is currently in the writing stage of his Ph.D. dissertation in Image Processing at Polytechnic University.

Professor Oudjehane began his teaching career as a mathematics instructor in Long Island University and he eventually headed the Mathematics Center at LIU as acting director until 1991.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Professor Pinto received his bachelor's degree in Computer Science from Hunter College and his master's degree in Business Administration from Baruch College.

Professor Pinto also has an undergraduate degree in Physics from the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and completed all course requirements for a master's degree in Physics from the Brazilian Center of Physics Research in Rio de Janeiro.

Prof. Pinto has his Ph.D in Computer Science from the CUNY Graduate Center. His research interests lie in intelligent networks, semantic Web, and Web services.

title: Professor
bio:
Dr. Ashwin Satyanarayana received his MS and PhD degrees in Computer Science from SUNY-Albany. Before joining City Tech, he was a Research Software Developer at Microsoft, where he worked on Microsoft's search engine Bing.

He brings to City Tech many years of experience in different areas of data mining. His current interests are in Data Mining, Machine Learning, Data Preparation, Information Theory, Applied Probability with applications in Real World Learning Problems.

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Sam Shahidullah received the M.S. degree in Computer Science from The City College of New York / CUNY in 1997. He also received the M.S. degree in Mechanical Engineering and the Ph.D. degree in Technical Science from the Kharkov Polytechnic Institute, Kharkov, Ukraine, in 1982 and 1986, respectively.

Sam Shahidullah is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Systems Technology at the NYCCT, CUNY where he has been a faculty member since 2001.

bio:
Dr. Hamid Norouzi is a full professor in the Department of Construction Management and Civil Engineering Technology at New York City College of Technology where he has been a full-time faculty member since 2011. Dr. Norouzi serves as the Director of Undergraduate Research at City Tech, and holds a joint appointment at the CUNY-Graduate Center in the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences (EES) as doctoral faculty. Prof. Norouzi completed his PhD in Civil Engineering (Water Resources, remote sensing) at the CUNY- Graduate Center. His research interests lie in the area of using GIS and satellite remote sensing observations in various geoscience and earth system sciences. It includes using satellite information in climate studies, urban climate, environmental justice, studying lakes, soil moisture estimation, precipitation, and estimation of soil freeze/thaw states.

Professional Experience

Professor Villatoro is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Construction Management and Civil Engineering Technology. She teaches a variety of courses in the civil engineering major including statics, strength of materials, concrete, steel, soil mechanics, and foundations. She has served as a Faculty Mentor for multiple students participating in the Emerging Scholars Program.

Professor Villatoro coordinates Peer Led Team Learning (PLTL) in Statics, a freshman semester course previously known for low student performance and a high rate of withdrawal. PLTL a pedagogical approach where students participate in workshops facilitated by peer leaders. She is currently directing a peer advisement program to increase retention of female students in engineering technology programs. The program includes monthly advisement meetings, workshops on professional development including resume building and mock interview sessions. The program aims to improve academic performance and provide them with the personal and professional skills necessary to graduate with their AAS degree within two years.

In collaboration with Professor Samaroo in the Chemistry Department she launched a STEM outreach project at Daniel Hale Williams elementary school in Brooklyn. The program was developed in alignment with the Next Generation Science Standards and blends the daily curriculum with engineering lessons. The program provides STEM exposure to a highly underrepresented population.

Professor Villatoro continues to practice her Engineering skills through private consulting. She provides services which include geotechnical reports, foundation design and support of excavation design in accordance with the requirements of the NYC Building Code.
