title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Hosni Auji is an Assistant Professor of Emerging Media Technology specializing in Game Design and Development.

Hosni's main research focuses on the design and development of accessible gaming experiences founded upon experimental concepts, often trying to find the boundaries of "fun." His approach favors a strong understanding of design fundamentals and a willingness to consciously subvert them in order to challenge conventions and expectations. While he considers himself to be design-focused, he has also taken on different roles in the game development process including, but not limited to, programming, 3D/2D Art, UX/UI, and motion graphics.

His work has been nominated for various indie game awards, including IGF and IndieCade, and has been exhibited and/or showcased at both galleries and festivals in New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, London, Milan, Amsterdam, Beirut, and Tokyo, among others.

Hosni received his MFA in Game Design from New York University. Prior to that, his background was in visual design. After completing his bachelor's in Graphic Design from the American University of Beirut (Lebanon), Hosni co-founded a design studio, receiving both design and administrative experience in areas such as branding, web interfaces, wayfinding systems and interactive installations. He also holds a diploma in Film Production from Prague Film School (Czech Republic).

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Allison Berkoy is an Assistant Professor of Emerging Media Technology, in the Entertainment Technology Department at New York City College of Technology. She heads the Physical Computing concentration, connecting software and hardware with digital and physical media, for creating tangible interfaces and interactive experiences.

Allison’s practice-based research explores the communicative potential of physical-digital environments when combined with mutable storytelling and media. These works take the form of interactive installations, electronic sculptures, and networked audiovisuals; driven by code, sensors, and human bodies. With participatory and absurd narratives, Allison’s installations become stages for performance that test the boundaries and etiquette of human-machine interaction as well as human-human relationship. As a designer, she has developed interactive, audiovisual installations for live events, museums, architecture, and gaming projects.

Allison completed her MFA in Electronic Arts at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, with a focus on interactive and immersive time-based media. Her earlier roots are in performance, with a masters in Performance Studies from New York University and a bachelors in Theatre from Northwestern University.

title: Chair
bio:
Susan Brandt is the Chair of the Entertainment Technology department at New York City College of Technology, CUNY. She earned a Master of Fine Arts degree from University of Southern California and a Bachelor of Arts from California State Polytechnic University Pomona.

She was the Technical Director for USDAN Performing Arts Center in the summer of 2008. She has been lighting modern dance since 1990. She was the resident lighting designer for Rudy Perez from 2001 to 2006. She was the resident lighting and sound designer for Theatre USC-USA at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival in 2000, 2001, and 2005. She also has created the sound design for LA Women's Shakespeare Festival productions of "A Winter's Tale," the "Tempest," and "Merchant of Venice." Sue was the Chair of Southern California Section of USITT from 2003 to 2008.

Sue Brandt's current research involves analysis of existing fire codes as they relate to live entertainment.

title: Associate Professor
bio:
John McCullough is the Technical Director and Associate Professor of scenery and fabrication in the Entertainment Technology Department at New York City College of Technology. His focus is on stage machinery and automation. Teaching duties include: drafting, scenery construction, technical direction, rigging and welding.

In the summer, he is the Technical Director for New York Stage and Film's Powerhouse Summer Season of new work in Poughkeepsie, NY.

John earned his MFA in Technical Design and Production at the Yale School of Drama.

title: Professor
bio:
Dr. David B. Smith, Professor of Music and Media Technology in the Entertainment Technology Department, is an award-winning composer, sound designer, inventor, educator, and researcher. His work focuses on sound, music, and media technology, immersive systems, and AI-assisted creative practice. He was the founding chair of the Entertainment Technology Department at City Tech (2003–2014) and served as Dean of the School of Professional Studies (2014–2022). Currently, he serves as Artistic Director of the Center for Holistic Integration (CHI). With over four decades of experience, he has contributed to performance, composition, virtual instrument development, interdisciplinary research, and curriculum innovation. He has created programs across multiple disciplines that bridge technology, the arts, business, health sciences, and emerging media. He has created curricula across multiple disciplines, focusing on integrative and interdisciplinary programs that bridge technology, the arts, business, health sciences, and emerging media.

At City Tech, Dr. Smith has played a pivotal role in securing major funding, including a $780,000 Alfred P. Sloan Foundation grant for music technology infrastructure, a Made in New York endowment to support promising students in the entertainment technology field, and an NSF TUES grant recipient. Dr. Smith is a leading contributor to the Balanced Blended Space (BBS) framework and its application to collaborative AI, quantum music research, and mixed-reality performance environments.

Dr. Smith is internationally recognized for his pioneering work in live performance virtual orchestra systems. In the late 1980s, he co-developed the first virtual orchestra technology in partnership with Dr. Frederick Bianchi, leading to groundbreaking applications in opera, theater, and immersive events—including the world’s first virtual orchestra in professional opera (Hansel und Gretel, 1990) and a 320-speaker immersive concert at Telecom’99 in Geneva.

As co-founder and Director of R&D at Realtime Music Solutions, Dr. Smith has led the development and deployment of the Sinfonia orchestral enhancement system, which has been used in hundreds of thousands of productions, including such high-profile clients as Broadway, West End, Cirque du Soleil, the Bernstein Foundation, the Gershwin Foundation, and many national and international tours.

His artistic work as a violinist, keyboardist, and composer bridges multiple genres—from classical to commercial to experimental—and he has designed sound for over 150 theatrical productions. His innovations in real-time music systems continue to evolve, now encompassing research in AI-human collaboration, gestural control systems, and quantum-aesthetic generative frameworks.  He was composer for the acclaimed documentary short 13 Drivers Licenses, which has garnered dozens of awards and has been in multiple venues around the world.

Dr. Smith is currently leading research in Quantum Music as part of a broader set of investigations into Collaborative AI, exploring how artificial intelligence can function as a creative partner across music, design, education, and systems thinking. His projects include the development of the Balanced Blended Space (BBS) framework, the Blended Reality Performance System (BRPS), and interdisciplinary efforts involving virtual environments, immersive sound, AI-mediated storytelling, the Blended Reality Performance System (BRPS), and meta-integrative efforts involving virtual environments, immersive sound, AI-mediated storytelling, and immersive audio environments for autonomous vehicles in military applications in partnership with the Autonomous Vehicle Mobility Institute (AVMI). He is particularly interested in developing new paradigms to describe and manage the increasingly complicated combinative reality within which we live.

He holds U.S. and U.K. patents in music performance systems and continues to mentor interdisciplinary student researchers across music, computation, and emerging media.  he is currently working on multiple composition projects, including the multi-media performance work Dark Room, and a sequel to the Mozart opera Die Zauberflöte.

title: Professor
bio:
Ryoya Terao holds an MFA from Parsons School of Design. He is a Professor of Video Production in the Department of Entertainment Technology at New York City College of Technology. Born and raised in Tokyo, Japan, hiswork, which includes experimental films, narrative shorts, and documentaries, has been shown on NHK (Japan BroadcastingCorporation), PBS, YesNetwork, and other TV networks in the U.S.A. and abroad as well as at film festivals.

During recent years, Professor Terao has co-produced and/or directed dozens of documentaries focusing on human-interestsubjects. Currently, Professor Terao has been directing a two-part documentary series on Jewish life in Lichtenfels, asmall town in Germany. The first film, chronicles the discoveries of the 13 driver’s licenses in the county office ofLichtenfels in 2017. They had been confiscated from Jewish drivers in 1938. A group of local high school students andtheir teacher researched the fates of the Jewish license holders. They found out that five of them and their familieshad been murdered--eight escaped. Eventually locating some of the surviving Jewish descendants overseas and invitingthem to their ancestors’ hometown, intriguing friendships developed. The film “13 Driver’s Licenses” has been screenedat film festivals around the globe and has received multiple best documentary awards.

The second documentary is currently in production and will focus on Nazi crimes and the relationship between modern-dayJews and non-Jewish Germans. It addresses questions of guilt, restitution, and reconciliation.

For further info., please visit: https://openlab.citytech.cuny.edu/13dl/

Other works by Ryoya Terao include “Sled-Dog Dreams” about a sled-dog team from an animal shelter in Durango, Colorado;“Go Achilles!” on disabled athletes from around the globe; “Gun Runners” on gun-violence through the eyes of former gangmembers in New York; and “Klavierhaus” on immigrant brothers who import and restore antique pianos. With respect toenvironmental concerns, he worked on a documentary about asbestos litigations and in the process, discovered agroundbreaking historic document that led to compensations for asbestos-related diseases in Japan. He also directed“Bamboo Bicycle,” a story on an innovative bike studio in Brooklyn operated by three young men, hand crafting bamboobikes for eco-friendly New Yorkers and people in the developing world.

Professor Terao has interviewed renowned actors such as Robert DeNiro and Julie Andrews, artists, and sportspersonalities such as the legendary PR announcer for the Yankees, Bob Shepard, as well as political and governmentalfigures, including Romeo Dallaire, the Force commander of the UN Assistance Mission in Rwanda (played by Nick Nolte inthe film Hotel Rwanda.)

title: Associate Professor
bio:
Dr. Adam J. Wilson is Associate Professor and Director of Emerging Media Technology, specializing in Computer Music.

Dr. Wilson's main research focus is computational creativity in music improvisation: he develops software that enables computers to improvise music in collaboration with him and other human musicians. His work incorporates algorithmic music composition and real-time generative techniques. Dr. Wilson performs with his software experiments on the fretless electric guitar, an instrument that caters to his penchant for microtonality. He has performed/presented his work in Tokyo, New York, Paris, Montreal, San Diego, Washington D.C., Boston, Baltimore, Atlanta, Belfast, Palo Alto, and elsewhere. Dr. Wilson co-founded and serves as director of the  New York City Electroacoustic Improvisation Summit, an annual concert series — hosted by City Tech — featuring music by artists focused on the integration of music improvisation and real-time interactive computer systems.

Dr. Wilson holds a Ph.D. in Music Composition from the University of California, San Diego, where he first began developing software to facilitate real-time musical collaboration between computers and human performers. He earned a Master of Music degree from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, and a Bachelor of Arts from Oberlin College. He is permanently certified as a secondary school teacher by the University of the State of New York, and taught for several years in the public schools in the Bronx.

Before joining the faculty at City Tech and between stints in academia, Dr. Wilson accumulated eight years of experience as a software engineer, working primarily in web development and SaaS cloud applications for both start-ups and established companies in Boston and New York City.

title: Associate Professor
bio: Dr. Brahimi graduated from Polytechnic University in Brooklyn, New York with a Masters and a Ph.D. degree. He has an extensive teaching and industrial experience. Dr. Alyssa Dana Adomaitis is an Associate Professor in our Fashion Marketing program. She obtained her Ph.D. in 2002 from the University of Minnesota in the Social Psychology of Dress and Human Behavior and obtained her MBA, specializing in Marketing, from Long Island University/ - C.W. Post in 1997.

Her research area of interest is in the social psychology of dress, consumer behavior, and retail advertising. She investigates people's perception of dress, self impressions, impression management, along with the impact of advertising on consumers' behavior. Her latest research includes socially responsible advertising, and global sourcing and foreign policy and its impact on the fashion industry both domestically and abroad.

She has been employed with several different companies in the fashion industry, holding positions that include a visual merchandiser at Saks Fifth Avenue New York, a trend analyst at The Fashion Service and personal assistant to the CEO of Sun Country Airlines. She has also been a consultant to Fred Segal, Fashion Business Inc., and Le Mystere.

Sutton, PhD, is the author of Globalizing Ideal Beauty: Women, Advertising, and the Power of Marketing (Palgrave Macmillan, 2009, 2012) and Innovative Teaching, with Dr. Alfred Posamentier (World Scientific, 2021). An expert on innovation and advertising beauty, she has lectured widely on the subject at universities and at corporations, e.g., Unilever and Firmenich, and as an invited visiting professor at the University of Le Havre, France. Dr. Sutton is an Associate Professor at City Tech-The City University of New York, where she teaches business history, fashion, and beauty culture, and serves as an advisory board member of CUNY Startups; she is also a board member of the Austrian American Educational Cooperation Association, Vienna, Austria. Dr. Sutton is an adjunct associate professor at the Fashion Institute of Technology’s School of Graduate Studies where she teaches a seminar on the history of innovation in the beauty industry. She is a 2020 Fulbright Award recipient (Vienna, Austria) and her research has been supported by Duke University’s Hartman Center for Sales, Advertising, and Marketing History; the National Science Foundation; and the Hagley Museum’s Center for Business, Technology, and Society. Dr. Sutton is currently working on a book about innovation in fashion and beauty (forthcoming, 2025).

Praise for Globalizing Ideal Beauty:


"An empirically rich and beautifully written study of the complex and often contradictory roles that women and gender played in the history of American advertising.  This should be essential reading for all those interested in understanding in what ways gender, class and race matter to the projection of American commercial culture at home and abroad.”- Mona Domosh, Joan P. and Edward J. Foley, Jr. Professor, Department of Geography, Dartmouth College

"This absorbing book contributes to a growing body of sophisticated work about 20th century advertising. Sutton's study follows a group of avant-garde female copy writers, the J. Walter Thompson Women's Editorial Department, focusing particularly on the interwar years. Sutton shows how these class-conscious, professional, modern, feminist style-setting copywriters created 20th century cosmetics advertising in JWT's imperialist, hyper-masculine corporate culture." - Tani E. Barlow, Ting Tsung and Wei Fong Chao Professor of Asian Studies, History Department, Rice University

“The brilliance of Sutton’s well-researched book lies in the way she takes a case study approach to how female advertising copywriters contributed to the development of the burgeoning American beauty industry, and to many of the cultural and marketing issues that our industry continues to face today. The chapter on Pond’s, in particular, is highly recommended for its ability to illustrate the knock-on effect of one company’s marketing strategy on changing broader perceptions of femininity, race, and class. This sophisticated analysis really resonates with my graduate students who are marketing professionals in the beauty industry.” - Leslie Harris, adjunct instructor, Fashion Institute of Technology, and Global General Manager of SkinCeuticals, L'Oréal USA

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Caroline Darin is an Assistant Professor in the Career & Technology Teacher Education department at New York City College of Technology. Her passion for education stems from a deep reverence for the art of teaching and belief that learning at its core is a joyful practice. She spent 10 years as a high school physics and AP Environmental Science teacher and school leader at Brooklyn Preparatory High School, where she co-developed the award-winning Science Genius Program alongside Dr. Chris Emdin, integrating hip-hop pedagogy with science education. She spearheaded projects to enhance culturally responsive curricula, student empowerment, and mastery-based learning, with her work focusing on project-based and differentiated learning practices to support student engagement and rigor.

Dr. Darin completed her Ph.D. in Science Education at Teachers College, Columbia University, where her research explored contemporary gender equity in science classrooms using mixed methodologies. She is a contributing author to "From White Folks Who Teach In the Hood" (Beacon Press, 2024). She continues her work on gender equity in education within City Tech, especially in the context of engineering and design practices in education as a means to support culturally engaging teaching in New York City.

title: Associate Professor & Chair
bio:
Euisuk Sung is Department Chair and Associate Professor of Career and Technology Teacher Education (CTTE) at New York City College of Technology (City Tech), CUNY. He earned his bachelor's degree in computer science education and then worked as a software engineer at a startup company, where he contributed to projects including real-time remote control software and web-based video communication. After three years in industry, he chose to become an educator, a decision he found to be the most exciting and meaningful of his career. He taught in public high schools for nine years, authored five technology education textbooks, and led teacher training workshops. He earned his Ph.D. in Engineering and Technology Teacher Education from Purdue University. At City Tech, he designed a CS teacher education program and redesigned the technology education curriculum to align with STEL standards (ITEEA, 2020). His research interests include AI in engineering design, computational thinking, design thinking, the philosophy of technology, and a broad range of issues in career and technology education.

Gwen Cohen Brown DDS is a Professor in the Department of Dental Hygiene at the New York City College of Technology and a Fellow in the American Academy of Oral and Maxillo-facial Pathology. Dr. Brown has been faculty at the AIDS Institute since 1992 and the NY/NJ AIDS Education and Training Center since 1993. Dr. Brown provides continuing education on the topics of Infection Control, Oral Cancer and Emerging Medical Technologies, and Common Oral Lesions for licensed health care providers in NY and NJ where she represents and is sponsored by the NYSDOH, the NYSDOC, the AIDS Institute and the CDC.

Dr. Brown graduated with a Doctor in Dental Surgery degree from New York University College of Dentistry in 1988, followed by an Advanced Education Program in General Practice Dentistry, also at NYUCD in 1989.

She completed a three-year residency program in Oral and Maxillo-Facial Pathology at the New York Hospital Medical Center of Queens followed by a two-year sub-specialty fellowship in Oral and Maxillo-Facial Pathology at the Health Science Center SUNY Brooklyn Downstate Medical College/Kings County Hospital Medical Facility.

Dr. Brown has worked at NYCCT since January 2004.

She received her Associate in Applied Science degree in Dental Hygiene from Hudson Valley Community College, a Bachelor of Science degree in Nutrition from Queens College, and a Master of Science degree in Environmental and Occupational Safety and Health from Hunter College. In addition, she obtained a second Master of Science degree in Education from Queens College and has Permanent Certification in Education.

Her interests include instrumentation, infectious diseases, infection control and asepsis, mentoring, community service, teaching methodology and calibration. She has presented at local, national, and international professional events.

Prof. Dillon has served as chairperson of the Dental Hygiene Department of New York City College of Technology (NYCCT) for over 6 years. An alumna, she received her Associate degree in Dental Hygiene from NYCCT, after which she received her Bachelor of Science degree in Dental Hygiene from Columbia University. She obtained her Master of Arts degree in Health Education from Teachers College, Columbia University. Prof. Dillon is also a recipient of the 2010 ADEA Colgate Palmolive Company Allied Program Directors’ scholarship and a recipient of a one year fellowship at the ADEA Leadership Institute from which she graduated in 2011.

She has over thirty eight years of experience in clinical dental hygiene practice. Along with her clinical experience, she also has over twenty three years of experience as a dental hygiene educator (with an emphasis on Periodontology and Clinical Practice). She has taught Dental Hygiene at New York University and Hostos Community College and has also lectured nationally and internationally on topics such as infection control, periodontal classification, periodontal measurements and geriatric dentistry and has published articles on various topics.

As one of only three dental hygienists on the New York State Board for Dentistry (NYSBD), the governing body for discipline, licensure and legislation in New York State, she served two five year terms and now continues to serve as an extended member. She is an examiner for the Northeast Regional Board for Dentistry; and serves as a site visitor for the Commission on Dental Accreditation (CODA).

Prof. Dillon makes herself available for community dental workshops and career guidance and believes that to whom much is given much is required, hence her willingness to serve. Although she has been in the profession of Dental Hygiene for many years, Prof. Dillon continues to be passionate about her multifaceted career.

title: Chair
bio:
Anna Matthews is a Professor in the Dental Hygiene program. She is serving as the department chairperson beginning in August 2022. Prof. Matthews is a registered dental hygienist who graduated from the City Tech Dental Hygiene program in 2004. Before becoming a dental hygienist, Prof. Matthews earned her Doctorate in Dental Sciences at the Belarussian State Medical University in Minsk, Belarus. She immigrated to the US after completing her residency in pediatric dentistry in 2000.

Following graduation from the City Tech Dental Hygiene Program, Prof. Matthews worked in the private dental practice and continued her education at the College of Staten Island, CUNY, where she earned a Master’s degree in Neuroscience and Developmental Disabilities in 2011.

Prof. Matthews has taught Oral Anatomy, Pharmacology, Principles of Dental Hygiene Care-II and clinical dental hygiene. She had served as one of the dental hygiene clinic coordinators for three years prior to her current appointment as the chairperson. Prof. Matthews has published many articles on a variety of topics including emerging issues in dentistry and dental hygiene, novel pharmacotherapies of medical and dental conditions, microbiology of oral and systemic disease, student diversity in health professions, and educational innovations/technology in the classroom. Many of her publications were written in collaborations with colleagues within and outside CityTech. She has presented her research at regional, national and international conferences and is a frequent contributor to the Colgate Oral Health Network. Prof. Matthews is a member of the peer review panel for the peer-reviewed professional journal Dimensions of Dental Hygiene.

bio:
Professor Khrystyna Vyprynyuk, RDH, MS, is a proud New York City College of Technology alum. She received her Associate in Applied Science degree in Dental Hygiene in 2009, and a Bachelor of Science degree in Health Services Administration in 2016. Prof. Vyprynyuk earned a Master of Science degree in Health Science with a concentration in Higher Education from Nova Southeastern University, Florida, in 2021.

Since 2017, Professor Vyprynyuk has been a dedicated member of the Dental Hygiene Department. She first served as an adjunct lecturer and became Assistant Professor in January 2022. She currently serves as the Freshman Clinic Coordinator, guiding first-year dental hygiene students in developing their foundational clinical, communication, and patient management skills.

Prof. Vyprynyuk has extensive clinical experience and has worked alongside many specialists in periodontics, general dentistry, and cosmetic dentistry throughout her career as a registered dental hygienist in private practice.

In addition to her teaching and clinical responsibilities, Prof. Vyprynyuk has published multiple peer-reviewed articles and serves on the Peer Review Panel for Dimensions of Dental Hygiene. Prof. Vyprynyuk encourages student research and is engaged in mentoring students on their research projects and presentations.

title: Chair
bio:
Dr. Katherine Gregory is an interdisciplinary scholar–practitioner with 20 years of research, teaching, and social marketing experience. Prior to joining CUNY/New York City College of Technology, she provided methodological support and course-integrated instruction as the qualitative data analysis and survey design specialist to faculty, researchers and students at NYU. She spent over five years at the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene as its media evaluation researcher where she oversaw concept testing, evaluation of health media campaigns, exploratory research, and provided social marketing outreach strategies to program stakeholders.
Dr. Gregory has taught full and part-time in several disciplinary programs at US universities, including the University of Wisconsin-Parkside, Syracuse University, Nova Southeastern University, CUNY/John Jay College of Criminal Justice, and NYU. Her book, The Everyday Lives of Sex Workers in the Netherlands (Routledge, 2005), addresses working conditions, cultural practices and social agency of transgender and migrant sex workers. 
Dr. Gregory’s research concerns digital health technologies, health disparities and the impact of social marketing on health outcomes; social aspects of genomics, and critical research methodologies.

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Sitaji Gurung, MD, MPH, PhD is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Health Sciences at New York City College of Technology (City Tech) of the City University of New York (CUNY) and Program Director of the Health Sciences program. She joined City Tech in January 2022.

Prior to joining City Tech, Dr. Gurung was a Research Scientist at Hunter College and Lead of the U19-Scale It Up Recruitment and Enrollment Center (U19HD089875; PI: Naar), overseeing multi-site studies on adolescent and young adult HIV prevention and care. Over a decade at Hunter, she directed more than twenty NIH-funded research projects, developed nationwide mHealth and virtual care studies. She also taught Biostatistics, Research Methods, and Public Health courses across CUNY campuses, and mentored students and research staff.

At City Tech, Dr. Gurung focuses on curriculum innovation, integrating electronic health records (EHR) simulations, research software (SPSS, Qualtrics, NVivo), and a digital health microcredentials lab into coursework. She also launched the Journal Club Series and SPSS Workshop Series to expand student learning beyond the classroom. A strong advocate for open educational resources (OER), she has authored two OER textbooks and continues to advance the scientific field through publications in peer-reviewed medical journals and CUNY-supported research.

Professional Experience and Research:

Ms. Rodriguez gained her public health experience at the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) as a Special Assistant to the Chief of Staff. In this role, Ms. Rodriguez actively participated in internal and external projects to improve agency processes and facilitate collaborations with other City agencies to protect the health of New Yorkers. She assisted in the drafting of the agency-wide confidentiality policy. She was a key support to the DOHMH's partnership with the Department of Homeless Services to improve the health of homeless adults. Also, Ms. Rodriguez was the primary author of the Bureau of Tobacco Control's proposal for nomination to the 2007 American Public Health (APHA) Epidemiology Section Award, which was awarded to the BTC at the 135th annual APHA conference in November 2007. In the health care sector, Ms. Rodriguez has been involved in quality assurance projects at Bellevue Hospital Center, New York City; at the San Juan de Dios Hospital in Barcelona, Spain; and at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Her previous teaching experience includes seventh grade physical science at a New York City junior high school, as well as English as a second language and health and hospital administration at Eugenio Maria de Hostos Community College, CUNY.

Ms. Rodriguez's research interests include how language barriers impact health care access; the use of medical interpretation to improve health outcomes; bioethics, with special interest in the ethics of genetic testing; the role of minors in health care decision making; and school readiness.

About

Dr. Mery Diaz is a Professor in the Human Services Department at New York City College of Technology/CUNY (City Tech). She received her MSW degree from the Wurzweiler School of Social Work at Yeshiva University and her DSW degree from the School of Social Policy and Practice at the University of Pennsylvania.
Dr. Diaz teaches Introduction to Human Services, Health Issues of Children and Adolescents, Women’s Health, and Field Practicum courses. She is the Faculty Liaison for the CREAR Futuros Peer Mentoring Program funded by the Hispanic Federation and is a founding member of City Tech’s Hispanic Serving Institution steering committee. Dr. Diaz also holds a residency at the Doctoral School of Social Work at Rutgers University where she teaches a module on research through autoethnography.
Dr. Diaz is Co-Editor-in-Chief of Affilia: Feminist Inquiry in Social Work, a Sage Journal. Her scholarship focuses on young people's minoritized, racialized, and gendered experiences, education, school mental health, reproductive justice, critical feminism, social justice issues, and narrative approaches.

Professional Experience

I have been teaching at City Tech for the past sixteen years. I feel gratified that I have taught human service students many invaluable lessons and skills that will follow them for the rest of their lives. I believe that education can be fun, but at the same time I demand excellence from my students.

It is my hope that all of our human service students will reach for the "gold" as far as advancing in the profession. I encourage students to move from the Associate degree to the Bachelor of Science degree in human services. Beyond education at City Tech, I encourage students to go for a Master's degree and to consider going for a doctorate if that is consistent with their career goals.

I enjoy teaching Introduction to Counseling as well as group dynamics since counseling is a strong component of what student do in the field. My specialty is in the substance abuse field and I have a keen interest in understanding how depression and anxiety play a role in people's lives who are suffering from these disorders.

title: Professor
bio:
Dr. Benjamin Shepard is a professor of Human Services at City Tech. He received his master’s degree at the University of Chicago’s School of Social Service Administration and his PhD at the Graduate Center of the City University of New York, He was trained in psychoanalysis at the William Alanson White Institute of Psychiatry, Psychoanalysis and Psychology’s Intensive Psychoanalytic Psychotherapy Program.

Much of Dr. Shepard’s scholarship is based on the ethnographic study of social services and social movements. He is the author/editor of over ten books including White Nights and Ascending Shadows: An Oral History of the San Francisco AIDS Epidemic (Cassell, 1997) and From ACT UP to the WTO: Urban Protest and Community Building in the Era of Globalization (co-edited with Ron Hayduck) (Verso, 2002). The latter work was a non-fiction finalist for the Lambda Literary Awards in 2002. Recent works include Play, Creativity, and the New Community Organizing (Routledge, 2011), Queer Political Performance and Protest (Routledge, 2009) and The Beach Beneath the Streets: Contesting New York City’s Public Spaces (co-written with Greg Smithsimon) (SUNY Press, 2011), and Community Projects as Social Activism (Sage, 2014, Rebel Friendships, “Outsider” Networks and Social Movements (2015, Palgrave), Brooklyn Tides(Transcript, 2018), Narrating Perspectives on Childhood and Adolescence (Columbia University Press, 2019), Illuminations on Market Street(a story about sex and estrangement, AIDS and loss, and other preoccupations in San Francisco) (Ibidem Press, 2019), and Sustainable Urbanism: Case Studies in Dialectical Activism (Roman and Littlefield, 2020).

In 2010, he was named to the Playboy Honor Role as one of twenty professors “who are reinventing the classroom.” Since then Shepard has written a weekly blog on art, activism and urban space entitled “Play and Ideas” that’s read across the country. He has done organizing work with Occupy Wall Street, AIDS Coalition to Unleash Power, SexPanic!, RTS New York, Times UP, Rebel Clown Army, CitiWide Harm Reduction, Housing Works, More Gardens Coalition, Right of Way, and Times UP! One of the most important organizing campaigns of his life was the successful “no more 24” campaign to reduce the course load at City Tech.

Since 2016, he has served as chapter chair of the City Tech chapter of the Professional Staff Congress.

In 2015, Shepard was named Scholar on Campus at City Tech.

In 2019, Shepard’s poetry collection  “We are officially inside a Kafka story” Changing Seasons with the Ditchdigger in New York was named to the short list of the William Faulkner – William Wisdom Creative Writing Competition.

In 2017, his novel Trying to Know Julie, later renamed Illuminations on Market Street, was named as a finalist in the William Faulkner – William Wisdom Creative Writing Competition.

As a social worker, he has worked in AIDS services/activism for two decades, joining ACT UP Golden Gate in the early 1990’s, opening two congregate facilities for people living with HIV/AIDS, serving as deputy director for a syringe exchange program, all while remaining active in efforts to bridge the gap between direct action and direct services. Today, he remains involved in organizing efforts around transportation, HIV/AIDS, labor, public spaces and environmental policy. Dr. Shepard combines these experiences, along with his training, to frame his scholarship, community engagement and teaching.

You can follow his work via his weekly blog, Play and Ideas.

Why I study Human Services:

Throughout my years in college just outside of Los Angeles, everyone said do not go to South Central. It's too dangerous. Yet, the weekend we were to graduate, there was a riot there after the Rodney King verdict. As I watched flames pour into the sky above downtown, I wondered why we allow our cities to suffer with so much inequality and neglect. Why is it that it takes a riot to get people to pay attention? I realized that day, I wanted to do more than watch the flames. By recognizing the needs of people in their environment, social work considers a wide range of areas for social intervention, from direct services to direct action. Social workers do not just study poverty; we aim to do help do something about it. From housing to AIDS activism, the Settlement to the Anti-Apartheid movements there is a long tradition of social workers participating a wide range of movements which bridge the gap from individual to community needs. Much of the process begins with a healthy home and a meal. Social work and human services are about helping create healthy communities. This is my life's work.

Research Interests:

My research interests are in five overlapping areas: social movements, community organizing, sexual politics, labor, and social work practice.

  • Social movements: those related to creative play, globalization, social problems, and the public sphere, specifically tensions between public and private space, health, and welfare.
  • Community organizing on the city, state, national, and transnational levels.
  • Sexual politics: moral panics, deviance, social control, and democracy, with a particular interest in queer and critical theory in the study of sexuality.
  • Labor: black market economies, sex work, welfare reform, and the public sphere.
  • Social work practice, history, and methods: comparative models of the welfare state, social welfare policy, narrative, life history, ethnography, qualitative research methods, urban social work, resiliency, psychoanalysis, harm reduction and radical public health.

These research interests are reflected in six books, numerous book chapters, articles, and book reviews on the intersections of urban studies, gender studies, queer theory, social movements, struggles between direct service and community mobilization, and the dilemmas of anti-poverty work in a post-welfare neoliberal city.

title: Professor
bio:
Karen Goodlad is an Associate Professor specializing in food and beverage management. Recently she has taught Wines of the New World, Wine and Beverage Management, Perspectives in Hospitality Management, and Internship. In addition to her joy of teaching she is often found working with club leaders, most recently as the City Tech Tea Club Faculty Advisor.

Finding it important to continually increase her understanding of the teaching and learning practices, she has worked as the Co-director of First Year Learning Communities and before that as the Co-director of General Education for the Title V Grant, A Living Laboratory. Through these and other leadership opportunities, she facilitated seminars for full-time and part-time faculty focused on incorporating High Impact Educational Practices, place based learning and effective assessment measures.

Prof. Goodlad was named by Total Food Service as a Top Woman in Metro New York Foodservice & Hospitality in 2019 and 2020. She is Certified Specialist of Wine with the Society of Wine Educators where she is also a member. This certification is evidence of her passion for expanding her own knowledge about wine and beverage but also her desire to effectively teach the subject.

Prof. Goodlad is a proud and active member of Les Dames d’Escoffier New York, the premier international organization of women leaders in food, beverage, and hospitality. Supporting the organization's mission in support of education, advocacy and philanthropy she moderated the inaugural wine trends conference, The Next Big Sip.

Her academic publications highlight her work as an educator and cover topics such as place-based learning, the first-year transition to college, and wine education.

Professor Brigitte Malivert is a Pastry Arts Lecturer at New York City College of Technology (City Tech), where she integrates classical French technique with culturally engaged and contemporary approaches to pastry. A graduate of Ferrandi Paris, she draws on her experience in acclaimed New York kitchens, including The Modern and Marea, to bridge technical precision with creative exploration in her teaching.

Her research focuses on decolonizing pastry, examining how culinary traditions reflect and reproduce cultural narratives. Through this work, she seeks to expand the ways pastry can serve as a site for storytelling, identity, and critical engagement. In the classroom, Professor Malivert encourages students to use pastry as a medium for self-expression and as a pathway to professional and artistic success in a globalized food landscape.

In addition, she taught recreational cooking to food enthusiasts at Chef Works Cooking school, Zwilling Cooking Studio and held the position of lead recreational chef at the Institute of Culinary Education (ICE) in NYC.

title: Chair
bio:
Marissa Janel Moran is an attorney admitted to practice before the U.S. Supreme Court, New York State, New Jersey, and the United States District Courts. She received her B.A. in Economics from Fordham University and her law degree from Brooklyn Law School. While in law school she interned at the U.S. Attorney’s Office, Southern District of New York, and upon graduation, clerked for U.S. Bankruptcy Chief Judge Burton R. Lifland in the Southern District of New York. She later worked as an associate at two New York law firms, Kaye, Scholer, Fierman, Hays & Handler and Emmet, Marvin & Martin.

She is currently the chair of and a professor in the Law and Paralegal Studies Department, New York City College of Technology, City University of New York, where she has over 25 years of legal education experience creating and teaching courses such as Legal Technology, Forensic Science & The Legal Process, Legal Document Preparation, Legal Ethics and Professional Responsibility, and Theatre of Law. Prof. Moran has served as the college’s grievance counselor and has chaired the Faculty Student Disciplinary Committee. She has also taught business law courses as an adjunct clinical professor at New York University, Stern School of Business.

Prof. Moran has written several articles for the Legal Educator, a publication of the American Association of Paralegal Educators, and has spoken at several New York State Bar Association CLEs and Paralegal Educator National and Local conferences on such topics as Legal Technology, Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, and Forensic Science & Law. Her article on biometrics and facial recognition technology was featured as the cover article in the May/June 2023 New York State Bar Association (NYSBA) Journal.

Prof. Moran has served as a judge for the American Bar Association (ABA) Law Student Division for the Client Counseling Competition, Dispute Resolution/Mediation Competition, Arbitration Competition, and the National Appellate Advocacy Competition; the Cardozo Law School Monrad G. Paulsen Moot Court Competitions, the International Moot Court Honor Society, Oxford Competitions, BMI Entertainment and Media Moot Court Competitions, and the Monroe Price Media Law Moot Court Competitions, the We the People High School Competitions; and Mock Trial NYC High School Tournaments.

She was a member of the NYSBA Task Force on Artificial Intelligence, and is currently the Vice Chair of the NYSBA Committee on Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies; the Vice Chair of the NYSBA Committee on Technology and the Legal Profession; and a member of the NYSBA Committee on Continuing Legal Education, NYSBA Committee on Committees, and the ABA International Law Section, Privacy, Cybersecurity and Digital Rights Committee.

title: Chair
bio:
Dr. Emerson Ea earned a BS in Nursing from the University of St. La Salle, in the Philippines, an MS in Adult Health from Long Island University-Brooklyn, a DNP from Case Western University, and a PhD from Duquesne University. Dr Ea has more than 20 years of experience in academia as a classroom and clinical instructor and in leadership positions. He has established faculty development, mentorship and interdisciplinary programs that support faculty to become regional and national leaders in education, scholarship and practice. He has led curricular innovations such as the integration of Design Thinking in an undergraduate curriculum. Dr. Ea is also an accomplished scholar with a focus on immigrant health and health equity. Currently, he is co-investigator of the Community Engagement core of an NIH P50 Center, the Rutgers-NYU Center for Asian Health Promotion and Equity (CAHPE), focused on addressing health inequities in the Asian American and Pacific Islander community in the New York-New Jersey area. He was Primary Investigator of previous studies on aging, immigrant health, hypertension among Filipino immigrants, and nursing education. He has widely published and presented his work in peer-reviewed journals, book chapters, and lay publications, and local and international conferences. Dr. Ea is also a recipient of numerous honors, awards, mentorships, fellowships, grants, and leadership positions in professional and community organizations. Most recently he served as a Health and Aging Policy Fellow in Washington, DC from 2022-2023 working with the US Department Health and Human Services.

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Michelle is graduated from Fairfield University with a Bachelor of Science in Nursing and a Minor in Psychology in 1995. She then continued her education at Hunter College where she received the dual degree of a Masters in Nursing and a Masters in Public Health with a concentration in Community Health Education in 2004. She has worked as a Registered Nurse in major institutions including New York University Medical Center on a medical/surgical unit, New York Presbyterian Hospital Weill Cornell Medical Center in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit and the Cardio-thoracic Intensive Care Unit, Phelps Memorial Hospital in the Intensive Care Unit. She further diversified her experience and skills as the director of a licensed home care agency and as a visiting nurse in the community. Michelle Cafaro Gellar joined the Nursing Department at New York City College of Technology in the Spring of 2009 where she has been teaching and has been promoted to Course Coordinator of the Foundations of Caring Nursing course. She teaches in both the theory and clinical sections with beginning Nursing students, in addition to the RN-BS students in Urban and Community Health classes. She has chaired several major committees within the Nursing Department. She participates in simulation with the students for clinical experiences. She maintains her New York State Registered Nurse license, is certified in Basic Cardiac Life Support, is a member of the New York State Nurses’ Association and the National League for Nursing Accrediting Commission. She continues to practice as a Registered Nurse in the community to maintain her clinical skills and remains current and updated in the technology and trends in healthcare.

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Professor Kontzamanis is an assistant professor and the Program Coordinator in the Department of Nursing’s Baccalaureate Program. She currently teaches Case Management: Role and Process. She has taught Leadership and Management, Community Health Nursing, and clinical sections of Urban Health.

Professor Kontzamanis has a BS in Nursing from Hunter College, an MA in Nursing Education from New York University, and a PhD in Nursing from the CUNY Graduate Center. Her research area of interest is cultural competence. Before coming to City Tech, she was an Assistant Professor at Long Island University and Vice President of Clinical Operations at Visiting Nurse Regional Health System. She has taught at St. Francis College in Brooklyn Heights and has held administrative positions at Metropolitan Jewish Health Systems. She has extensive experience in Community Health Nursing, Leadership and Management and Case Management.

Professor Kontzamanis is on the Nominating Committee of the Northeast Chapter of the Transcultural Nursing Society and a member of the National League for Nursing and Sigma Theta Tau International, Upsilon Chapter.

title: Senior CLT
bio:
Ms. Shi Li-May Li is a Senior CLT (College Lab Technician) in the Department of Nursing. She is responsible for managing and overseeing class and lab activities in the nursing lab and N.E.L.L. (Nursing Enhancement Learning Laboratory). Within these class and lab activities, Ms. Shi Li-May Li performs technological tasks for students and administrative requests for faculty.

Ms. Shi Li-May Li received her Masters of Science in Information Systems from The City College of New York. She also has Associate degree in Nursing for Registered Professional Nurses (RN). In clinical experience, Ms. Shi Li-May Li has worked over 15 years in the Medical Intensive Care Unit, Open Heart Surgery Unit, Maternity and Newborn Center.

Currently working as a Senior CLT (College Lab Technician), Ms. Shi Li-May also is an adjunct faculty member in the Department of Computer Systems Technology. Through supporting the Department of Nursing and teaching in the Department of Computer Systems Technology, Ms. Shi Li-May Li will continue to play an active role in serving this academic institution.

title: Professor
bio:
Dr. Rafferty completed her pre-licensure nursing education at State University of New York Plattsburgh; a Master of Arts in Nursing from New York University; a Master’s in Public Health (MPH) from Columbia University, Mailman School of Public Health; and a Doctorate in Nursing Practice (DNP) from Case Western Reserve Frances Payne Bolton School of Nursing.

Dr. Rafferty is currently a Professor at City Tech and the former long-time Chair of its Nursing Department.  A social advocate throughout her career, Dr Rafferty published U.S. Congressional Testimony on the Homeless, testified before the New York State Senate and New York City Council on environmental issues, and received the Circle of Mercy Award from Mercy Center, a South Bronx-based community organization. From 2013 to 2025, she served with the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN) as a Peer Evaluator, Team Chair, and member of the Evaluation Review Panel.  Dr. Rafferty currently volunteers with the Marian K. Shaughnessy Leadership Academy and the Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health, Global Consortium on Climate and Health Education, Global Nurses Working Group.

title: Associate Professor
bio: Professor Lisette Santisteban RNC-OB, MS-Ed, an Assistant Professor is a registered professional nurse licensed in New York and New Jersey. She is a certified within her clinical specialty of maternal child health from the National Certification Corporation (NCC). Professor Santisteban is a peer-reviewed author who has presented her work at the annual Educational Summit through The National League of Nursing, the premiere nursing organization. The Golden Key International Honor Society has recognized her for her outstanding academic success while continuing her education in a doctoral program. The International Nurses Association as a World Wide Leaders in Healthcare has also recognized Professor Santisteban as a Top Nursing Educator in New York, New York. She served as a mentor on the Mayor’s Center for Economic Opportunity/New York City Health & Hospitals Corporation Nurse Mentoring Program as well as a member of the National Association of Hispanic Nurses, and serves the college through several committees. Professor Santisteban is a proud to be alumni of City Tech’s Associate Degree Program and is honored to be a faculty member of the program that launched her successful career.

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Celeste Waddy is currently an Assistant Professor in the Department of Nursing. She is the Coordinator of Psychiatric Nursing and also teaches this course in the third semester of the Associate Degree Program. Her specialization is Psychiatric and Community Health Nursing.

Professor Waddy graduated from New York City Technical College with an Associate Degree in Nursing. She received a B.S. in Nursing from St. Joseph’s College and continued her studies there, receiving a M.S. in Nursing, specializing in nursing education. She was a recipient of the Senator Patricia K. McGee Nursing Faculty Scholarship. Celeste was awarded certification as a Legal Nurse Consultant from Long Island University. Professor Waddy is a Nonviolent Crisis Intervention® Senior Certified Instructor from the Crisis Prevention Institute, and conducts training every semester to nursing students.

Prior to entering academia, Celeste worked as a Nurse Educator for the Department of Psychiatry at Mary Immaculate Hospital in Jamaica, New York. She has many years of nursing experience in long term care, management, leadership, community health, and psychiatric nursing.

Professor Waddy is active on several committees for the Nursing Department, the College and the Community. She serves on the Alumni Board of Directors and is a Mentor for the Alumni Association. Professor Waddy presented before the National League for Nursing on several occasions. She also presented at CPI International Instructors’ Conference regarding a one year research study she conducted at the College. She has peer reviewed publications, including local, national and international presentations. Celeste has a passion for nursing, enjoys teaching and loves imparting knowledge to her students.

Education:

Dr. Lillian Amann is a distinguished alumna of New York City College of Technology (City Tech), where she embarked on her journey in radiologic science and medical imaging. In 2008, she successfully graduated with an Associate Degree in Applied Science, marking the beginning of her illustrious career in healthcare.

Eager to further her education and expertise, Dr. Amann earned a Bachelor’s Degree in Applied Science in Radiologic Sciences from Florida Hospital College of Health Sciences in 2011. Her relentless pursuit of knowledge continued with a Master’s Degree in Radiologic Science, focusing on education, from the esteemed Thomas Jefferson University in 2014.

In August 2024, Dr. Amann completed her Doctorate in Health Sciences with a focus on education in healthcare professions from Nova Southeastern University. This accomplishment underscores her dedication to advancing the quality of healthcare education.

Professional Experience:

With 15 years of experience in radiologic science and medical imaging, Dr. Amann has been a significant asset in both clinical and academic environments. She brings her extensive experience to her full-time role as a lecturer at City Tech.

As a clinical instructor, Dr. Amann has played a pivotal role in shaping the careers of aspiring radiologic technologists, offering hands-on training and mentorship that has been instrumental to the success of countless students.

Teaching Expertise:

Dr. Amann’s passion for teaching spans a diverse range of courses, including introductory radiologic technology, patient care, and imaging modalities. Her multifaceted teaching approach ensures students receive comprehensive, real-world education to meet the challenges of modern healthcare.

Certifications:

A certified Red Cross instructor, Dr. Amann specializes in basic CPR, first aid, and AED training for adults and children. Her dedication to safety exemplifies her commitment to healthcare preparedness and community welfare.

Leadership in Service Learning and Academic Excellence:

Dr. Amann leads her students in participating in the annual "Making Strides for Breast Cancer" event, raising over $5,000 annually for research and awareness. She also pioneered Lambda Nu, City Tech’s first radiologic technology student honor society, fostering academic excellence and professional growth.

Her journey from City Tech student to full-time lecturer and doctorate holder highlights her unwavering commitment to the field of radiologic science and education. Dr. Amann continues to inspire students and colleagues alike, emphasizing teamwork, community service, and academic excellence.

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Professor DeVito received his Bachelor of Science degree from St. Joseph's College in Brooklyn and his Master of Arts degree from Stony Brook University.

Professor DeVito has an extensive background in Cross-Sectional Anatomy and Patient Care. He currently teaches Advanced Patient Care/Pharmacology and Advanced Cross-Sectional Anatomy in the Baccalaureate program. In the Associates program he teaches or has taught Patient Care and Management, Radiographic Physics, Advanced Radiographic Procedures, Clinical Education IV, Clinical Education V and Seminar. He is also the Co-Clinical Coordinator of the program with over twenty-five years’ experience as an educator.

Professor DeVito has been a member of the Association of Educators in Radiologic Technology since 1992. He has served on numerous elected board positions of that society including president. He has also served on the board of the New York State Society of Radiologic Sciences and has been a member since 1991. Prof. DeVito has also served on committees for the American Society of Radiologic Technologists and currently serves on their CRTA committee (Committee on R.T. Advocacy Region 9 Subcommittee).

title: Senior CLT
bio:
Jodi-Ann Douglas, MSRS, R.T.(R)(ARRT) is the Senior College Laboratory Technician (CLT) for the Department of Radiologic Technology & Medical Imaging. She maintains the equipment and assists both students and faculty in the radiology learning and energized x-ray laboratories.

Ms. Douglas is an Alumni of New York City College of Technology, and is a certified and licensed Radiologic Technologist in the State of New York.

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Dr. Jennett M. Ingrassia is a nationally certified Registered Radiologic Technologist with the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists and is licensed to practice radiography in both New York and New Jersey. She received her initial radiography training and certification at a hospital-based program, and both her AAS in Radiologic Technology and BS in Medical Imaging from Thomas Edison State University. She holds a Master of Science in Radiologic Sciences, Education Track from Midwestern State University and a Doctorate in Education in Organizational Leadership in Higher Education from Grand Canyon University.

Dr. Ingrassia has been in the radiologic technologist profession for over 35 years. She has been a Past President of the New Jersey Society of Radiologic Technologists (NJSRT) and has been a member of the Board of Directors for many years. Dr. Ingrassia has been a Delegate to the American Society of Radiologic Technologists (ASRT) and has served on numerous ASRT committees, most recently the Baccalaureate Curriculum Revision Committee. She is also a graduate of the ASRT Leadership Academy and the ASRT Leadership Academy for Educators. Dr. Ingrassia has published several research articles in Radiologic Technology, the professional journal for the ASRT. She has also served as a site visitor apprentice to the Joint Review Committee on Education in Radiologic Technology.

Dr. Ingrassia has been involved in radiography education for over 30 years. She has previously been employed as a didactic and clinical instructor at the radiography program in Helene Fuld Medical Center as well a clinical laboratory technologist at Passaic County Community College. She also held faculty positions at Essex Community College and Bronx Community College and was the Clinical Coordinator at the Muhlenberg Schools for Radiologic Imaging. She has instructed courses in patient care, radiographic exposure, and pathology and all levels of radiographic procedures. While at City Tech, Professor Ingrassia has taught Introduction to Radiologic Technology, Procedures I, and the Radiography Seminar class. She has also taught the Pathology and, more recently, the Capstone courses in the department's Baccalaureate program. Dr. Ingrassia is also the advisor to the REM RAD Club.

Dr. Ingrassia has lectured at the national level and at many state and local conferences. She holds memberships in the New York State Society of Radiologic Technologists, New Jersey Society of Radiologic Technologists, Association of Educators in Radiologic Sciences and the American Society of Radiologic Technologists.

title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Professor Lespinasse currently teaches Introduction to Radiologic Technology & Medical Imaging, and Radiation Protection & Applied Radiobiology. She coordinates curriculum planning and scheduling for the department and has directed several funded projects for equipment purchase.

With over 25 years of teaching experience, Professor Lespinasse has taught a variety of courses in the medical imaging discipline including Radiographic Physics, Advanced Radiographic Studies, Imaging Modalities, Seminar, Radiographic Pathology, Radiographic Procedures and Positioning, Pediatric Radiography, Medical Terminology, Health Care Ethics, Patient Care, and Mammography. She has also taught Legal Issues in Health Care in a baccalaureate degree program at St. Francis College and served for six years as program director of The Long Island College Hospital School of Radiologic Technology.

Professor Lespinasse is a frequently invited speaker at professional conferences both locally and nationally. Her areas of concentration and interest include Teaching and Learning, Classroom Management, Service Learning, Mammography, and Bone Densitometry. She currently serves on various Educational Advisory Boards and has held other Board positions in professional organizations including Chairperson, President, President Elect, Vice President, and Recording Secretary.

Professor Lespinasse received her Bachelor of Science degree from St. Francis College, her Master of Science degree from Central Michigan University, holds advanced certification in mammography and awarded a Doctoral Equivalency in Radiologic Technology and Medical Imaging in 2006.

bio: Professor Ryan Rowe teaches lab sections for Patient Care and Radiographic Positioning I, II & III, and is also a clinical instructor. title: Professor
bio:
Professor Sarkar teaches Capstone Leadership Roles in Medical Imaging and Advanced Medical Imaging I and II. He is an internationally renowned professional in radiologic safety, quality and neuroimaging. He has joined New York City College of Technology as the Director of Baccalaureate Program in Radiological Science.

With over 30 years of professional experience, Professor Sarkar has worked in several academic and for-profit institutions as a teaching faculty, medical physicist, radiologic technologist and radiology manager. He has trained radiologic technologists, physicians, fellows and medical residents in imaging physics, physical chemistry and clinical image quality. He has worked with equipment vendors and medical organizations for future imaging developments. He has published his work in peer-reviewed journals in Materials Science, Engineering, Radiology, Neurology and Surgery.

Professor Sarkar received his combined Bachelor’s and Master of Science degree from Birla Institute of Technology & Science and a Nuclear Physics Specialization from Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics in India. He obtained a Master’s degree in Physics from University of Pittsburgh and a PhD degree in Chemical Physics from Washington State University in USA. During his postdoctoral training at Texas A&M and at the Medical School of Arkansas he learned and developed imaging techniques in the early 90’s applicable to industrial imaging. He has served as a medical physicist faculty at Texas Osteopathic School of Medicine in Dallas and at Harvard Medical School in Boston. For the past three decades he has focused primarily on medical and related materials imaging and has developed advanced spectroscopic and imaging methods as a scientist and radiologic technologist.

Professor Sarkar is a reviewer of several biomedical journals and a reviewer of biomedical research grant applications.

title: Associate Professor/Instruction, Reference
bio:
Nora Almeida is Associate Professor in the Library Department at New York City College of Technology and a member of the library’s instruction team. She teaches library credit courses including the place-based interdisciplinary course Learning Places. She is the subject specialist for Architecture, Human Services, Theater, and World Languages. Prof. Almeida also leads library outreach and instructional design activities and you might find her screenprinting with students during club hour or working to integrate library resources into educational technology platforms.

Prof. Almeida is an interdisciplinary scholar, social practice and performance artist, and embodied researcher. Her art explores intersections of archiving, environmental investigation, and spatial disruption. Recent public artworks—Last Street End in Gowanus (2021), Land Use Intervention Library (2022), and Open Water (ongoing)—focus on relationships between people and environmentally disturbed, post-industrial waterfront spaces. Nora was a 2022 Water Connector with Works on Water, a 2021 Social Practice CUNY Faculty Fellow, and a recipient of a Brooklyn Arts Council Local Artist Support Grant in 2024 and of Puffin Foundation Environmental Arts Grants in both 2022 and 2024. She is a 2024-2025 printmaking apprentice with Shoestring Press.

She is a long-time collaborator with the videographer iki nakagawa. Since 2022, they have been working on the site-specific public art project and archival activation experiment Creek: Two Cavities of the Heart based at Coney Island Creek. She is co-founder of Hydrofeminist Map Collective with the somatic researcher and artist andrea haenggi, architect and scholar Estefania Mompean Botias, and urbanist and designer Jordan Packer.

Prof. Almeida is also a long-time volunteer at Interference Archive, an exhibition space, community center, and open-stacks archive of social movement ephemera in Brooklyn. She teaches as a Visiting Professor at the Pratt Institute School of Information.

bio:
Kel R. Karpinski (they/he) is Associate Professor and the Information Technology and Interlibrary Loan Librarian in the Ursula C. Schwerin Library at NYC College of Technology.

Kel does research in American Studies, Cultural Studies and Queer Studies. Their work focuses on performance, masculinity and desire in queer texts from WWII to early Gay Liberation in the 1970s, especially as it relates to sailors and hustlers in Times Square and how these texts map queer desire onto the city.

Kel also works in the medium of zines, disseminating their research creatively through the practice and art of zinemaking. They are coorganizer for the NY Queer Zine Fair and also serve as Vice President for the NY Metro regional chapter of the American Studies Association (NYMASA).
